items.title: Mohsen Marzouk n’assistera pas aux obsèques de sa mère
items.description: Mohsen Marzouk a annoncé hier, samedi 17 octobre 2026, dans un poste Facebook, le décès de sa mère, Salha El Abdi, «le grand olivier qui nous a nourris de son huile, nous a protégés des loups de la nuit, nous a appris le principe et la connaissance et nous a hissés sur la colline pour qu’on ne perde pas la voie du soleil», a-t-il écrit sur le ton de la poésie, l ' affaire de sa vie à côté de la politique. «Elle est décédée paisiblement dans son sommeil au terme d’une vie entièrement vouée au combat qu’elle a mené seule, entourée de ses trois enfants, après le décès de son époux alors qu’elle n’avait pas atteint ses trente ans» , écrit encore l’ancien ministre-conseiller politique au cabinet du président Béji Caïd Essebsi, fondateur et président du parti Machrou Tounes. «Je ne serais pas à ses côtés pour creuser la terre avec mes mains et la livrer à la poussière et à l’obscurité, mais elle ne sera pas seule, puisqu’elle sera entourée de Rakia et Sarhane» , son frère et sa sœur qui accompagneront la défunte à sa dernière demeure. Marzouk a voulu rappeler ainsi qu’il a quitté la Tunisie au lendemain de la prise de pouvoir de Kaïs Saïed et le début des procès politiques et qu’il vit aujourd'hui en exil, à l’instar de nombreux anciens responsables politiques tunisiens. I. B. L’article Mohsen Marzouk n’assistera pas aux obsèques de sa mère est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Candidature de Macky Sall au secrétariat général de l’ONU : le RUR salue un retrait « pour l’unité »
items.description: Le Réseau des Universitaires Républicains (RUR), structure qui se réclame de l'Alliance pour la République, a réagi dans un communiqué à la décision de l'ancien président Macky Sall de retirer sa candidature au poste de Secrétaire général de l'Organisation des Nations Unies. Ce retrait intervient au lendemain du vote informel du 16 octobre 2026 . Dans son texte, le RUR présente ce geste comme un sacrifice consenti pour favoriser la recherche d'un consensus au sein du Conseil de sécurité. Il y voit un acte placé « au-dessus de son ambition personnelle », qui « témoigne de sa hauteur de vue, de son sens des responsabilités et de sa grandeur ». Le titre du communiqué parle d'un « homme d'État ». Une candidature portée au nom de l'Afrique Le RUR exprime sa « profonde reconnaissance » à Macky Sall pour avoir porté « une candidature qui dépassait sa personne ». Selon lui, elle traduisait l'ambition légitime de voir l'Afrique jouer un rôle accru dans la gouvernance mondiale. Le réseau énumère les axes d'une vision des Nations Unies fondée sur la rénovation du multilatéralisme, la promotion de la paix, une meilleure prise en compte des préoccupations des pays en développement et la construction d'un ordre international plus juste, plus équitable et plus inclusif. Des remerciements aux soutiens Le communiqué salue ensuite les efforts diplomatiques déployés, notamment ceux d'Évariste Ndayishimiye, président en exercice de l'Union africaine, ainsi que l'engagement des États africains et des partenaires internationaux. Le RUR remercie aussi le président de la République du Sénégal, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, pour son soutien, de même que la diplomatie sénégalaise. Cette mobilisation, estime-t-il, rappelle que les grandes ambitions internationales du Sénégal « peuvent et doivent rassembler les forces vives de la Nation ». Le réseau adresse enfin ses remerciements aux Sénégalaises et aux Sénégalais, de l'intérieur comme de la diaspora, ainsi qu'aux universitaires, aux intellectuels et aux acteurs de la société civile mobilisés. Engagé « dès les premières heures » derrière cette ambition, il se dit convaincu que les idées défendues par Macky Sall « conservent toute leur pertinence face aux défis mondiaux ». « Ni le renoncement à une ambition ni la fin d'un engagement » Le RUR refuse de voir dans ce retrait un point final. « Le retrait d'une candidature ne signifie ni le renoncement à une ambition ni la fin d'un engagement », écrit-il. Il affirme que l'ambition de l'Afrique de prendre toute sa part dans la conduite des affaires du monde, « jusqu'aux plus hautes responsabilités au sein des Nations Unies », reste entière et doit se poursuivre. Le réseau salue enfin la volonté de Macky Sall de continuer à défendre les idéaux du multilatéralisme, de la paix, de la solidarité et de la coopération entre les peuples, au service de l'Afrique et de la communauté internationale. Il lui renouvelle « son estime, sa reconnaissance et son soutien »

2027: APC chairman predicts 70% North’s votes for Tinubu
items.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, says the North will deliver more than 70 per cent of its votes to President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Yilwatda spoke on Saturday in Abuja at the opening of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a political pressure group mobilising support for Tinubu and the APC. He described the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity to renew Tinubu’s mandate, citing infrastructure projects, political appointments and inclusive governance. The APC chairman expressed confidence that northern voters would support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the region had benefited significantly from his administration. He listed road projects across the North, including the Trans-Saharan Super Highway, covering routes from Benue through the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Akwanga, Jos, Maiduguri and Biu. “I can’t mention all of them, but President Tinubu has done wonderfully. He has covered all the geopolitical zones in the North in terms of road projects,” he said. Yilwatda said the administration was also undertaking railway and healthcare projects across the region, including health centres and free medical services for pregnant women. He identified the appointment of northerners to key political positions as another reason the region should support Tinubu’s re-election. The APC chairman urged supporters to secure votes for Tinubu at the grassroots, expressing confidence in their ability to deliver the projected 70 per cent. “Even if in our hometown alone we can win our polling units for President Tinubu, we have over 70 per cent of the vote in the North, just us alone in our polling units. “So we have no reason not to return Tinubu. Therefore, I move that he should be returned for the second time,” Yilwatda said. The post 2027: APC chairman predicts 70% North’s votes for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan suspends Iran trade corridors over 'security, smuggling concerns'
items.description: GWADAR/QUETTA: Pakistan has suspended trade with Iran through the official Gabd-Rimdan (250) and Taftan border crossings, it emerged on Saturday. The Ministry of Commerce issued a memorandum on Friday, seen by Dawn , withdrawing its earlier order [No. 9(3)2017-Iran] dated Oct 3 with immediate effect. Shahid Rind, adviser to the Balochistan chief minister on media and political affairs, said the “purpose of the temporary closure of the Pak-Iran border is to address security concerns, prevent smuggling, and make the border system more effective”. In a statement on X, Rind refuted “rumours being spread on social media” regarding the closure and urged the public not to pay attention to unverified information. The Balochistan official stressed that the move was “necessary to improve the security situation and administrative affairs on both sides of the border”. Rind affirmed that “progress continues between the high officials of both countries to resolve administrative issues” related to the border. “In the context of the current progress, the Pak-Iran border is likely to reopen soon,” he said, adding that a coordinated system was being established to improve border affairs and prevent smuggling. Meanwhile, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei also said the closure was temporary, Iran’s state-run Irna reported . However, he attributed the move to “technical issues” and said the two countries were in consultations to resolve the problem and restore normal operations. Separately, the Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry (QCCI) has also advised its members and businesses involved in trade with Iran to stop placing new import and export orders until further notice. Hundreds of freight vehicles carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), rice, fresh fruit and other essential commodities have reportedly been stranded on both sides of the border. According to Iran-based Wana news agency, passenger traffic through the Rimdan–Gabd crossing remains operational. It quoted Syed Hossein Hosseini, director general of the Iranian Transit Office, as saying that commercial operations at the border crossing had been halted. The Gabd-Rimdan crossing had become a major route for meeting Pakistan’s energy needs, with over 4,000 tonnes of LPG reportedly imported daily through it. Exports of Pakistani products, particularly rice, had also surged in recent months, generating millions of dollars in foreign exchange. Sources in the trade and energy sector warned that the closure could aggravate LPG shortages in Karachi and other parts of the country. The Taftan route was already facing disruptions amid unrest in Balochistan. The suspension of supplies through Gabd-Rimdan could push up LPG prices in the open market. Local traders and the chamber have warned that the disruption could cause not only substantial losses to the national exchequer and jeopardise the livelihoods of many but also an energy crisis. Since March this year, Islamabad and Tehran have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures , formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes , against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran war that has strained economies in the region and beyond. In early August, an Iranian delegation led by Trade and Industry Minister Mohammad Atabak visited Islamabad for the 10th session of the Pak–Iran Joint Trade Committee (JTC). The delegation also met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, with both sides agreeing to further expand trade ties by keeping border crossings open round the clock, improving logistics and harmonising customs procedures. The visit came a couple of months after it was reported that trade between Pakistan and Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing had come to a complete halt. According to Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry President Jiand Hoot, trade through the Panjgur and Mand-Radig border crossings was virtually non-existent because of poor road infrastructure and recurring incidents of arson and vehicle burnings.

items.title: Digging in Karachi for Red Line damages gas pipeline, disrupts supply
items.description: KARACHI: Gas supply to several areas of the metropolis was suspended during lunch hours on Saturday after a high-pressure pipeline was damaged during excavation work for the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line on University Road, adding to the miseries of residents in the affected areas. The disruption affected Gulshan-i-Iqbal, areas around Mazar-i-Quaid, parts of Garden, Saddar, Burns Road and several other localities. A spokesperson for the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) said that the high-pressure pipeline near the Gulshan-i-Iqbal telephone exchange on University Road was damaged at around 1pm during BRT construction activity. She said teams immediately reached the site and started repair work, which was completed by 5pm. “After completion of the work, gas supply was restored,” she said. Residents in the affected areas said the sudden suspension caused considerable inconvenience, particularly during cooking hours. Several households reported disruption in preparing afternoon meals, while commercial eateries and roadside hotels in Saddar and Garden saw a rush of customers as many people had no option but to dine out or take food home for their families. Domestic consumers complained that low pressure persisted even after the announced restoration time. Many families said they had to arrange food from nearby restaurants. “We had guests at home and the gas suddenly disappeared. We had to order biryani from a nearby hotel, which cost us extra besides causing embarrassment,” said Rozina Adnan, a resident of Saddar. items.title: Messi brace lifts Inter Miami to 3-1 win in Atlanta
items.description: Lionel Messi scored twice in the space of four minutes to lift Inter Miami to a 3-1 victory at Atlanta United on Saturday as the Herons’ MLS title defense continued to gain steam with the playoffs approaching. The 39-year-old superstar tops the Major League Soccer scoring chart with 25 goals, six ahead of Croatian striker Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Philadelphia’s Milan Iloski. At the same Atlanta stadium where Messi helped Argentina beat England in the World Cup semi-finals in July, Messi delivered two scintillating goals to secure Miami’s third straight victory. German Berterame, who put Miami up 1-0 in the 45th minute, turned provider, finding Messi who weaved through the Atlanta defense to unleash a left footed shot from the center of the box and make it 2-0 in the 56th minute. Four minutes later Messi struck again, breaking away on a pass from Luis Suarez and getting the better of hapless Junior Alonso to fire past Atlanta keeper Lucas Hoyos. Messi had helped put Miami on top shortly before halftime, heading the ball to Suarez who shook off his defender in the box and lofted a pass that Berterame nodded home to make it 1-0. Messi was credited with an assist, that saw him pull level with LAFC’s Son Heung-min atop the assists table. Messi is the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three straight seasons. Messi now has four goals in three matches since his emotional Argentina send-off. Miami, who clinched a playoff berth on Wednesday, won their third straight game under Cristian “Kily” Gonzalez, who took over as coach last month. Fafa Picault converted a penalty in the 89th minute to pull a goal back for Atlanta, but at second-from-bottom in the Eastern Conference Gerardo Martino’s team are running out of time to turn things around in time to reach the playoffs. – St. Louis streak ends – Elsewhere, St. Louis City’s MLS record-tying 19-match unbeaten streak ended with a 3-2 loss at Minnesota as Philadelphia’s undefeated run reached 15 matches with a 2-2 draw with Charlotte. Canadian Marcus Caldeira scored the game winner for Minnesota in the 86th minute after United fell behind early on St. Louis goals by Brazilian forward Rafael Navarro and South Korean winger Jeong Sang-bin. Aziel Jackson answered for Minnesota in the 49th minute and Kelvin Yeboah netted the equalizer in the 68th. St. Louis City, already headed to the playoffs for the first time since 2023, missed the chance to break the MLS unbeaten streak mark it now shares with Columbus, Dallas and Inter Miami. City also saw their MLS-record 21-match unbeaten streak across all competitions snapped. City had not lost an MLS match since falling 2-0 at Austin on May 3, with 13 victories and six drawn in the run. Philadelphia had won eight MLS matches in a row before the fightback home draw with Charlotte. Philadelphia lost 6-4 at Miami on May 24 but since then the Union have won 12 times and drawn three, taking 39 of a possible 45 points since Ryan Richter took over as interim head coach during the league’s World Cup break. items.title: Dele Cole: Life and times of eminent journalist, ambassador
items.description: By Osa Mbonu-Amadi, Deputy Editorial Board Chairman Eminent journalist, Ambassador Dele Cole, has passed on in a London hospital. Family sources told Sunday Vanguard that he died yesterday morning after a month in Intensive Care Unit, ICU. He was the Managing Director of Daily Times before being appointed Nigeria’s ambassador to Argentina and Brazil. Popularly known as P. D. Cole, he was one of the most consequential figures in modern Nigerian journalism, public administration, diplomacy, and political thought. A scholar, newspaper administrator, columnist, historian, businessman, and elder statesman, he helped shape the intellectual character of Nigerian newspapers and represented Nigeria abroad with distinction. Early life and education Patrick Dele Cole was born on August 4, 1940. He has often attributed his outlook to the values instilled in him in childhood: honesty, hard work, respect for elders, and contentment. His mother was a midwife, while his father was well educated; both placed a high premium on education. He began his schooling at St. Bartholomew School, Asata, in Enugu, where he reportedly walked four to five miles to school. He later received his secondary education in Eastern Nigeria and higher education in Western Nigeria. Because of that experience, Cole described himself as one who had a broad, pan-Nigerian formation. Cole proceeded to the University of Otago in New Zealand and later to the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom, where he obtained a doctorate and spent three years as a fellow. He also had an academic stint at the University of Pennsylvania in the United States. Scholar and public servant On returning to Nigeria, Cole entered the civil service and worked in the Cabinet Office. He became associated with the intellectual circle around General Olusegun Obasanjo during Obasanjo’s time as military Head of State, serving as a member of what became known as the Obasanjo Think Tank. His background in history, policy analysis, and public administration gave him an unusual combination of academic depth and practical statecraft. It was this reputation that brought him into the newspaper industry at a decisive moment in Nigerian media history. Transformation of the Daily Times Cole came into public prominence in 1975 when he was appointed a non-executive director of the Daily Times, representing government interests on the board. In 1976, he became Managing Director of the newspaper at a time when the institution was undergoing major political and organisational upheaval. The Daily Times was then one of the largest and most influential newspaper organisations in Africa, with numerous publications and subsidiaries, including Times Press and Niger Pack. Following the federal government’s acquisition of a controlling stake in the company, Cole’s immediate task was to restore stability, confidence, and professional harmony within the organisation. His tenure is remembered for several enduring achievements. Amongst those achievements are the fact that he rebuilt morale and strengthened the professional structure of the Daily Times after a period of crisis. He also established Nigeria’s first newspaper Editorial Board modelled on American practice, separating systematic editorial opinion-making from the traditional features-department approach. Cole brought leading intellectuals, including Dr. Stanley Macebuh, Doyin Abiola, Olu Akaraogun, Dele Giwa, and Sam Oni, into the paper’s editorial culture. He defended editorial independence, notably backing editors who resisted pressure to suppress sensitive stories. He continued the Daily Times tradition of investing in staff training and human-capital development. Under Cole, the newspaper retained its hard-hitting editorial voice while also achieving commercial success. His administration is widely credited with helping the Daily Times regain its stature as a leading African newspaper. Champion of editorial independence Perhaps Cole’s most important legacy in journalism is his defence of the newspaper as an institution of accountability. Although he entered the Daily Times as a government-appointed director, he did not behave as an instrument for muzzling the press. Instead, he protected editors and insisted that the newspaper’s primary loyalty was to its readers and to the public interest. A celebrated example involved the Sunday Times and a planned lead story on Nigeria Airways. When government officials sought to stop publication, the editor refused. Cole backed the editor, reinforcing the principle that editorial decisions should not be dictated by political convenience. He also stood with Daily Times editor Tony Momoh in the celebrated confrontation over the Senate’s attempt to summon the editor over publication of a Senate document. The episode became a landmark in the struggle for press freedom and editorial autonomy in Nigeria. Role in the emergence of The Guardian After his time at the Daily Times, Cole played an important behind-the-scenes role in the emergence of The Guardian in 1983. He supported the selection of the newspaper’s founding editor and helped ensure that its early editorial output met the standards of a serious, ideas-driven publication. Cole later became associated with The Guardian’s Editorial Board, where he continued to contribute to public debate. His influence helped make the newspaper’s editorial board one of the most respected in Nigerian journalism. Diplomatic career Cole later moved into diplomacy. He served as Nigeria’s Ambassador to Brazil from 1990 to 1993, during the administration of General Ibrahim Babangida ,retd, and was also accredited to Argentina. His diplomatic service was marked by the same directness that characterised his journalism. In later interviews, he explained that he considered it his duty to remind political leaders of their promises and obligations, even when doing so was unpopular. He argued that public officials owe the people honesty, especially on commitments that are ethical and part of their declared programmes. He subsequently served as Special Adviser on International Relations to President Olusegun Obasanjo, bringing his diplomatic experience and policy expertise back into the heart of government. Politics and public intellectual life Cole has also been active in Nigerian politics. In the early 1990s, during the aborted Third Republic, he sought the presidency on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP). Although he did not win the party’s presidential ticket, his candidacy reflected his long-standing engagement with questions of leadership, governance, and national unity. Beyond partisan politics, he has remained a prominent public intellectual. Through newspaper columns, interviews, and public commentary, he has spoken forcefully on corruption, federalism, economic management, youth unemployment, local-government autonomy, pensions, and the responsibilities of leadership. He was also a celebrated columnist for Vanguard Newspapers, where his sharp, informed and often provocative interventions enriched public debate. Personal life Cole was married to Mina Dugoabere Cole, a devout member of the Redeemed Christian Church. She died in England in October 2021 after a prolonged illness. Her death deeply affected him, but friends and associates noted his resilience and his return to public life in the years that followed. He cherished his role as a father and grandfather and often described his family as one of his greatest blessings. In his 85th-birthday interview, he said his children had become more successful than he had hoped, adding that this fulfilled one of his deepest prayers. Enduring legacy Ambassador Dele Cole’s life illustrated the power of the public intellectual in national development. He moved with ease between the university, the newsroom, the diplomatic service, business, and politics, yet journalism remains the field in which his influence is most visible. Throughout his life, Dele Cole remained an active participant in national discourse. His career stood as a reminder that journalism, at its best, is not merely the reporting of events but a civic vocation: one that demands courage, intellectual honesty, and an unwavering commitment to hold power accountable. Reactions Meanwhile, prominent journalists, yesterday, reacted to his demise, saying he helped create a more confident and intellectually vibrant newspaper culture in Nigeria. Editor of Vanguard Newspapers and President Nigeria Guild of Editors, NGE, Eze Anaba, said Cole’s tenure at the Daily Times was pace-setting. His words: “Dele Cole was, in my view, one of the pioneers of modern Nigerian journalism. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he brought Dele Giwa back to Nigeria from the United States and, together with other brilliant journalists such as Stanley Macebuh, helped create a new, more confident and intellectually vibrant newspaper culture. “His tenure at the Daily Times was pace-setting. He assembled a remarkable generation of journalists and helped lay the foundation for the energetic, bold journalism that Nigerians enjoyed in the late 1980s and early 1990s. “Beyond his newspaper-management record, he was a celebrated columnist whose contributions to Vanguard enriched national discourse. “He was a pace-setter, and we will miss him hugely. That is the best way I can describe him. I cannot assess him as a politician or as a diplomat. He served Nigeria as Ambassador to Brazil, among other roles. “But I can speak confidently of his record as a brilliant newspaper manager: he changed the face of Nigerian journalism and left an enduring mark on the profession.’’ On his part, Provost, Nigerian Institute of Journalism and former Editor-in-Chief and General Manager, Vanguard Newspapers, Mr. Gbenga Adefaye, said Cole would be remembered for his consistency, courage, intellectual depth and skill as a media manager. His words: “P. D. Cole, Dr. Patrick Dele Cole, as he was formally known , was “the man from the Cabinet Office,” the description by which many in the media also knew him. He was a great man who came in to manage the Daily Times, especially during the difficult transition years from military to civilian rule. “He was appointed Managing Director of the Daily Times in 1976. He is particularly remembered for bringing in outstanding journalists and thinkers, including Dr. Stanley Macebuh and Dele Giwa, and for helping to reposition the newspaper at a time of considerable institutional and political pressure. “Beyond the Daily Times, he had a wide media reach and was central to the founding of The Guardian in 1983. Working with Alex Ibru, Stanley Macebuh and Segun Osoba, he helped build what became one of Nigeria’s most substantial and influential newspapers. “He will be remembered for his consistency, courage, intellectual depth and skill as a media manager. He was also a significant public servant and politician. Under President Olusegun Obasanjo from 1999, he served as Special Adviser to the President on International Relations. Earlier, he had served Nigeria as Ambassador to Brazil and also to Argentina. “I cannot say more than that for now. May his soul rest in perfect peace. It is a great loss and a great miss; that generation is indeed passing away.” Also, Dean, Faculty of Communication and Media Studies, Lagos State University (LASU), Professor Jide Jimoh, said: “The death of Dr Patrick Dele Cole (PDC) is a sad reminder that we are not going to get out of this world alive, but our legacies will remain long after we have left. “His contributions to journalism cannot be forgotten in a hurry. I observed him more closely when I was a Visiting Member of the Editorial Board of The Guardian Newspapers and he was one of the intellectual powerhouses in that newspaper. “His contributions would most likely change the direction of an editorial because of his erudition. “He delivered his points without arrogance or force but with the sole aim of illuminating dark spots in thoughts. He will be greatly missed by Nigeria and, more regrettably, by those of us who have benefitted from his versatility. Adieu, Dr PDC.’’ Vanguard News The post Dele Cole: Life and times of eminent journalist, ambassador appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ram Leela Temple in Dera Ismail Khan sealed amid demolition fears
items.description: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: The authorities here on Saturday locked and sealed the historic Ram Leela Temple in Rahim Bazaar days after civil society activists intervened to stop the demolition of the heritage building for the construction of a commercial plaza at the site. The building had earlier been sealed by Assistant Commissioner Hamid Siddiq following public protests and work at the site was stopped, said local sources. The latest development came as civil society representatives and members of the Hindu community held a joint meeting to discuss the reported move to demolish the temple. The participants condemned the proposed construction and called on elected representatives to raise the issue in the National Assembly. The meeting, held at the office of civil society president Sohail Ahmed Azmi, was attended by former MPA and Hindu community representative Kishore Kumar, social worker Muhammad Nauman and others. The participants said the Ram Leela Temple was among around 400 buildings in Dera Ismail Khan identified as cultural heritage properties by the Evacuee Trust Property Board. They expressed concern over any move to demolish the temple and said civil society, the business community, writers and heritage advocates would resist any action that could damage the city’s historical heritage. The participants also alleged that the relevant authorities had allowed construction of a commercial plaza at the site despite questions over their legal authority to do so. They called for an inquiry into the matter and said complaints would be submitted to the district administration, the NA speaker, the archaeology department and other relevant authorities. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: ‘I’ll be back in few weeks ‘- Chelsea’s goalkeeper Martinez after undergoing surgery
items.description: Emi Martinez has undergone surgery following a head injury sustained during Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League victory over Everton on Saturday, with the goalkeeper saying he expects to return in a few weeks. The Argentina international, 34, suffered the injury in the 67th minute at Hill Dickinson Stadium when he collided with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite while attempting to punch an Everton free kick away from his penalty area. Both players received treatment on the pitch, but Branthwaite recovered quickly, while Martínez required extended medical attention from Chelsea’s medical staff and paramedics. The goalkeeper was eventually stretchered off the pitch while receiving oxygen and was replaced by 21-year-old Mike Penders in the 75th minute. The lengthy stoppage resulted in 11 minutes of added time at the end of the match. Martinez later shared a photograph of himself in a hospital bed on social media, reassuring fans that his operation had been successful. “Thank you all for the messages, the operation went well. The most important thing is that we won and with a bow at 0. We’ll be back in a few weeks,” he wrote. Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso had earlier confirmed that Martinez was conscious when he left the stadium and had been taken to hospital for precautionary examinations. “For now, we need to wait,” Alonso told reporters. He added: “It was a concussion, but more than that. I saw just one clip, but we’ll have to wait.” Chelsea secured all three points through two goals from Pedro Neto, ending Everton’s unbeaten start to the campaign and keeping their first clean sheet of the season. Neto dedicated the victory to the injured goalkeeper, telling TNT Sports: “We are really pleased. Shame for Emi, but we wish you all the best. This win is for him.” Everton manager David Moyes also expressed concern over Martínez’s condition, saying he had not seen the incident clearly from the dugout. “I just said to TV, I’ve not seen the Martínez injury yet, so I hope he’s fine. I really do. I couldn’t even see from the dugout. It just looked as if it was a sharing ball in between a couple of people. I don’t know what else happened,” Moyes said. Reflecting on Chelsea’s performance, Alonso praised his players for their defensive discipline and ability to withstand pressure away from home. “I’m really pleased with the performance, with the win, with the clean sheet,” Alonso said. “There are many positives to build on from today. We knew it was going to be a hard challenge to win in this stadium, but we did many things to deserve the win. I think we got many things right. We were very professional, very solid, and it’s good to have this feeling to win this way. “We needed to feel like we could win in this way — being solid, being strong, looking in control and going through difficult moments. “In the first half, there were moments where there were corners and throw-ins and you need to overcome these moments. It’s very hard in the Premier League to have full control of the game but you need to make sure you don’t lose your shape or your condition, and today we did that really well. items.title: Japan to launch historic round-trip mission to Mars moon
items.description: Japanese scientists are preparing a mission to Mars’s moons to retrieve samples that could help unlock the origins of the solar system and life on Earth, in what aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region. The unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe, a collaboration with US and European space agencies as well as numerous universities and tech companies, could also help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration. The flagship H3 rocket carrying the MMX is set to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Centre on Tuesday at 4:41 am (12:41am PKT), according to the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). The spacecraft will arrive near Mars one year later, where it will orbit its moon Phobos for up to three years before landing and collecting at least 10 grams (0.35 ounces) of material from the surface. A rover dubbed IDEFIX — the French name for the comic hero Asterix’s dog — will first conduct surface observations aimed at ensuring a safe landing. “The sampling (from) Phobos is of course the world’s first, but it means… this is the first round trip to the Martian system,” MMX’s project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu told AFP . JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a “natural space station” by establishing the requirements for a round trip to Mars — something “essential for crewed Mars exploration”. It will also observe the Red Planet’s moon Deimos, although it will not land on it, before returning to Earth. Impact or capture JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born. One theory for the origin of the Martian moons — the “giant impact” hypothesis — is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars. The “capture” hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids captured by Mars’s gravity. Determining which is right will help reveal “how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets”, JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun — Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. “MMX will shed light on the transport mechanisms that delivered water, volatiles, and organic compounds from the outer solar system to the inner rocky planet region — processes that may have played a key role in making these worlds habitable,” said Patrick Michel, a French astrophysicist working on IDEFIX. “If Phobos and Deimos are indeed remnants of these early delivery systems, they may hold clues to the origins of life itself, or, to be more correct, to the transport of the materials that were key to the emergence of life on rocky planets,” he told AFP . Deep in the ‘gravity well’ MMX is a collaboration with France’s National Centre for Space Studies (CNES), the German Aerospace Centre (DLR), Nasa, the European Space Agency (ESA), and about 20 universities and tech companies. The development of the spacecraft’s landing legs was particularly difficult, as gravity on Phobos is extremely weak, JAXA scientists say. Japan’s unmanned Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM) — the “Moon Sniper” — tipped over after touching down on Earth’s Moon in 2024, but still transmitted data and survived several two-week lunar nights. Japan also has experience in bringing back samples from space, including JAXA’s unmanned Hayabusa-2, which returned 5.4 grams of rock and dust collected from an asteroid several hundred million kilometres from Earth in 2020. One of the differences between JAXA’s past asteroid probes and the MMX mission is that this time “we have to travel very close to Mars and return”, which means escaping the planet’s heavy gravity, Kawakatsu told reporters. Phobos orbits about 6,000 kilometres above the Martian surface. “Going deep into what we call the ‘gravity well’ is difficult,” Kawakatsu said. China’s mission US and Chinese space agencies have been racing to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth. Nasa’s Perseverance rover , which has been roaming the Red Planet since 2021, has already collected samples. The mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by the US Congress in January. China, meanwhile, has announced its Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 — potentially before the MMX’s return. JAXA scientists say sand and rocks from Phobos may offer a wider variety of samples than those on the planet itself, especially if it was formed by a collision between a celestial body and Mars.

items.title: Mali : le FLA cherche des appuis à Benghazi et à Abou Dhabi
items.description: Isolé et en manque de moyens, le Front de libération de l'Azawad (FLA) d'Alghabass Ag Intalla cherche à diversifier ses soutiens à Benghazi et auprès de Abou Dhabi. Selon des sites spécialisés, une délégation du FLA a rencontré à Benghazi Saddam Haftar , numéro deux de l'Armée nationale libyenne, pour solliciter équipements et coopération militaire. Le contact s'appuie sur une médiation libyenne qui avait permis la libération de deux paramilitaires russes détenus par le FLA depuis juillet 2024. Chacun poursuit ses propres objectifs : le FLA cherche à renforcer ses capacités militaires et à desserrer son face-à-face avec Bamako , tandis que Saddam Haftar entend étendre son influence au Sahel. Mais l'enjeu dépasse la Libye. Abou Dhabi, principal parrain du camp Haftar, offre à Benghazi un accès que le FLA peut vouloir exploiter, en contournant les médiations traditionnelles. Un motif sérieux d’inquiétude pour l’Algérie Pour l’Algérie, l’implication de réseaux liés aux Émirats à nos frontières est un motif sérieux d'inquiétude. Outre l'installation de relais étrangers dans notre profondeur stratégique, le FLA risque de se faire instrumentaliser au service des agendas hostiles de puissances extérieures. La Russie utilise la Libye orientale comme un point d’appui logistique pour ses activités en Afrique. Un soutien militaire de Saddam Haftar au FLA contre l’Africa Corps, qui est présente aux côtés du gouvernement malien, risquerait donc de contrarier un partenaire dont le camp Haftar dépend encore. Dès lors, comment expliquer que le Front de libération de l’Azawad se tourne vers Benghazi pour obtenir des équipements et une coopération militaire ? Saddam Haftar pourrait-il réellement aider les indépendantistes touaregs à combattre les forces russes qui soutiennent Bamako, au risque de compromettre ses propres relations avec Moscou ? Ou cette démarche relève-t-elle plutôt d’un jeu d’influence dans lequel chacun cherche à renforcer ses positions sans remettre en cause ses alliances stratégiques ? Par ailleurs, la question s’inscrit dans une rivalité régionale plus large, où l’axe Émirats arabes unis-Maroc-Israël cherche à renforcer ses positions politiques, économiques et sécuritaires en Afrique du Nord et au Sahel. Pour notre pays, cette convergence nourrit la crainte de voir des puissances hostiles multiplier les relais dans notre environnement immédiat afin d’entraver notre action et de réduire notre influence traditionnelle dans la région. Les liens militaires entre Rabat et Tel-Aviv, l’ancrage émirati auprès du camp Haftar et l’expansion des réseaux d’Abou Dhabi au Sahel alimentent cette perception. L’article Mali : le FLA cherche des appuis à Benghazi et à Abou Dhabi est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Bac : la nécessaire réforme (par Daouda Mané)
items.description: Depuis la grande concertation nationale organisée du 28 au 31 janvier 1981, communément appelée les États généraux de l’éducation et de la formation (Egef), soit plus de quatre décennies, le Sénégal n’a de cesse de réformer son système éducatif. L’objectif reste le même : s’ouvrir aux progrès scientifiques et technologiques du monde moderne, tout en étant enracinée dans ses valeurs et traditions. Ce, d’autant plus que le système se caractérise par l’inadéquation entre la demande et l’offre éducative, entre formation et emploi. En témoigne le fort taux de chômage dans le pays. Selon les données de l'Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (Ansd), ce taux de chômage élargi s'établit à 19,1% au 2e trimestre de 2026, soit une légère hausse par rapport aux 19,0% de la même période en 2025. Environ 33,5 % des jeunes de 15 à 24 ans sont classés comme NEET (Ni en emploi, ni en éducation, ni en formation). (Cf. Ansd, Enquête emploi, 30 septembre 2026). En réalité, dans le système éducatif, domine un réel sentiment de « bourrage de crâne », tant il est caractérisé par des programmes encyclopédiques, une surcharge horaire et mentale et surtout un décalage avec le marché de l’emploi. D’où le débat, malgré l’adoption de l’Approche par les compétences (Apc : qui vise à rendre l’élève acteur de son apprentissage) depuis quelques années, sur l’allègement des programmes scolaires, à travers une révision constante des curricula. Certes, depuis 1995, des mesures phares ont été prises. Il s’agit, entre autres, de l’augmentation du nombre de séries avec l’avènement du baccalauréat franco-arabe en 2000, du baccalauréat agricole et agro-alimentaire en 2003 et du baccalauréat arabe en 2013 ; l’orientation des formations supérieures vers les Sciences, la Technologie, les Sciences de l’Ingénieur et les Mathématiques (Stems) ; la réforme des baccalauréats séries techniques qui a transformé trois filières (G, T1 et T2) sur les sept actuelles en deux baccalauréats technologiques (Sciences et Technologie d’Economie et de Gestion et Sciences et Technologies industrielles pour le développement durable)… Toutefois, il faut reconnaître que le baccalauréat connaît encore des faiblesses, dont le manque de pertinence, de validité, absence de banque d’épreuves validées structurées, le manque d’efficacité, de fiabilité, etc. (Cf. Tdr de l’atelier de réflexion sur le Baccalauréat, MESRI, octobre 2017). C’est là toute la pertinence de la refondation initiée par les nouvelles autorités qui repose sur plusieurs réformes, notamment celle du baccalauréat – premier diplôme de l’Enseignement supérieur – qui doit être appliquée d’ici le 30 janvier 2027. Il faut simplement rappeler que cette volonté politique date de près d’une dizaine d’années, précisément en 2017. (Cf. Tdr de l’atelier de réflexion sur le Baccalauréat, MESRI, octobre 2017). Le nouveau pouvoir aura le mérite de la finaliser, même si la date d’entrée en vigueur n’a pas été annoncée. Séries regroupées, socle commun, fin des cloisons, modernisation, frais d’inscription revus à la hausse, etc. Telles sont les grandes lignes de cette réforme qui prévoit donc une réduction drastique des séries qui passent de 18 (dont certaines, les séries arabes, sont restées inactives : S1, AR et S2-AR) à 4. Ainsi, les 18 séries seront ramenées à 4 parcours : Sciences, numérique et innovation qui a regroupé les actuelles séries S1, S2, S1A, S2A et F6 ; Technologies et industries (Stidd ET S3) ; Agriculture, environnement et agro-alimentaire (S4 et S5) et Economie, gestion et sciences sociales (Steg et l’ensemble des séries littéraires). Pour les frais d’inscription, ils devront passer de 5.000 FCfa (bloqué depuis 2000 alors que le coût réel d’un candidat est de 32.000 FCfa) à 10.000 FCfa. (Cf. Sene-News du 26 septembre 2026). Autrement dit, on assistera à un allègement de la charge de travail et à une adaptation aux mutations actuelles afin d’offrir à nos étudiants un avenir prometteur. Une bonne nouvelle pour les acteurs, surtout les élèves qui apprennent des matières qui ne leur servent plus à grand-chose. daouda.mane@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Tinubu’s Northern support not a blank cheque — Shettima
items.description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has warned that growing support in northern Nigeria for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid is not a “blank cheque”, saying the administration must earn voters’ confidence through transparency, accountability and measurable results. Shettima spoke in Abuja on Saturday at the unveiling of the Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A) campaign head office and the inauguration of the group’s campaign structure for the 2027 presidential election. He said the growing political support for Tinubu placed an obligation on the administration and its supporters to explain the impact of its policies and reforms on Nigerians. “By now, I believe the north has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken,” the vice-president said. “Such confidence places an obligation upon us that no officeholder should ever underestimate.” Shettima said the administration must base its campaign for a second term on its record and demonstrate how another four years would advance the interests of Nigerians. “The mandate belongs to the people. We must account for its use and explain how another term would advance their interests,” he said. He added that northern Nigerians had nothing to fear from Tinubu’s second term, while stressing that elected leaders must remain accountable to citizens. ‘Nigerians have endured difficult adjustments’ The vice-president acknowledged that Nigerians had endured difficult economic adjustments, warning government supporters against dismissing public concerns or relying on political slogans to defend government policies. “Our citizens have endured difficult adjustments. We cannot pretend otherwise,” he said. “What we owe them is an honest account of the decisions taken, the gains achieved and the difficulties that persist. We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information.” He said the experiences of traders grappling with higher costs, graduates searching for jobs and families struggling with daily expenses should inform government decisions. “A failed policy enters somebody’s home as a missed meal, an unpaid school fee or an opportunity lost,” he said. Shettima described criticism as an essential part of democratic governance, saying the administration should remain open to ideas regardless of political affiliation, ethnicity, religion or region. “There is no democracy without critics. Progress demands that our assumptions endure the examination of those who disagree with us,” he said. He urged the A4A campaign structure to serve as a channel through which concerns from communities could reach government officials. “A complaint should travel from a community to those who can act upon it. The people who speak through this organisation deserve to know that somebody is listening,” he said. The vice-president identified security, economic opportunities, poverty reduction, education and stronger public institutions as key government priorities. “The farmer should be able to cultivate in safety. A child’s education should prepare that child for a productive life. Public institutions should give citizens confidence that effort can yield opportunity,” he said. He added that the responsibilities of governance would continue beyond the election campaign. “Even as elections impose a deadline upon persuasion, public service imposes no deadline upon our duty,” he said. Yilwatda urges North to back Tinubu, Shettima National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, urged northern Nigerians to support Tinubu’s re-election, citing Shettima’s leadership and what he described as the administration’s achievements. Yilwatda said the vice-president had fostered an inclusive political environment by bringing together people from different religious and ethnic backgrounds. “He has built an inclusive environment, bringing all of us together, ensuring that whether you are Christian, Muslim, whether you are of different faith, different religion, different tribe, he has brought us together under one shelter, always talking to us and engaging us,” he said. The APC chairman called for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket to be returned for a second term. “So we have a reason to back him, to support him, and the two of them, the joint ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Shettima, should be returned for a second term,” he said. Earlier, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin said the inauguration of the A4A structure came at a time when the North needed a trusted platform to mobilise support for Tinubu. Barau said the group would help communicate what he described as the administration’s achievements across the region. Akume, northern governors back second term Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the North should decide on the 2027 elections based on evidence and an assessment of the administration’s record rather than sentiment. Akume also called for the region’s influence to be harnessed to promote national unity and development. Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf, who spoke on behalf of northern governors, said the region would support the Tinubu-Shettima ticket based on the administration’s performance. He said the region’s support for the president would reflect a commitment to fairness, equity, unity and national progress. Former Jigawa State Governor and Director-General of A4A, Abubakar Badaru, said the group was established out of the conviction that Tinubu and Shettima had performed well and deserved another term. Badaru pledged to take the campaign for continuity and completion of the administration’s projects to communities across northern Nigeria. The event was attended by serving members of the National Assembly, ministers, presidential aides, heads of government agencies, former governors and other political leaders from the North. The post Tinubu’s Northern support not a blank cheque — Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dans l’huis d’un esthète de l’universel
items.description: Visiter « Les Dents de la mer », du nom de l’ancienne demeure du premier chef de l’État du Sénégal, c’est rencontrer l’intimité d’une personnalité autant nimbée d’une gloire perpétuelle qu’il est sempiternellement conspué. La maison, devenue « Musée Léopold Sédar Senghor » depuis 2014, loge encore aujourd’hui l’âme de ce « métis » de l’universel, qui affirmait son hybridité jusque dans son « mbind ». Avant de pénétrer l’ancienne demeure de Léopold Sédar Senghor, on est forcément tenté d’imaginer comment se dessine l’écrin d’un féru d’art et artiste lui-même jusque dans l’âme, politique jusqu’aux ongles, et humaniste de tout son verbe. La bâtisse, qui fait face à la mer, à Fann-Résidence, sur la Corniche ouest de Dakar, reste auguste malgré la menace de vétusté. Passé le seuil, on découvre un vaste domaine de 7.432 m2. Le calme dépare la pétaudière routière du dehors. L’air de l’intérieur est caressé par la brise marine, quoiqu’un peu fouetté par les klaxons et autres pétarades. Mais l’attention du visiteur est plus happée par la majesté de la résidence, conçue par l’architecte Fernand Bonamy et construite entre 1975 et 1978, qui répond au parallélisme asymétrique. La surface bâtie de 880 m2 est entourée d’un jardin qui ne l’est resté que sur l’avant-cour, avec son baobab-fétiche qui fait sentinelle. Derrière et sur le côté, les arbres touffus qu’ils forment presque une haie de brise-vent. Les céans du poète de la Négritude Un lourd portail en bois massif donne sur l’espace de vie des « Dents de la mer », devenue « Musée Léopold Sédar Senghor » depuis 2014. Senghor, avec Colette son épouse et leur fils Philippe Maguilen ont aménagé ici après son départ du pouvoir en janvier 1981. Le visiteur admire, dès le vestibule, une grande étagère de collection. Le meuble compartimenté garde les souvenirs de voyages et autres présents d’homologues du premier chef de l’État du Sénégal indépendant. Laissée en l’état du rangement du couple, la collection démontre l’idée de la civilisation de l’universel que chérissait Senghor, tout en exaltant le Berceau de l’humanité. Au tout sommet de l’étagère, trône une Tête de pharaon Toutânkhamon. Oui, l’Égypte pharaonique, civilisation pionnière. Elle domine le reste des trésors issus de tout le monde : statue Bamiléké, présent d’un monastère de Normandie, vase de Corée du Sud, relique Dogon, traces de Cabo Verde, de Japon et Taïwan, des États-Unis, etc. Deux autres bibliothèques renseignent la culture hybride de Senghor. Avec deux exemplaires du coran et de la bible qui partagent le même coffret, Léopold exprime sa foi ancrée mais tolérante. Deux statuettes de guerriers ceddo (ou cedo, corrigerait probablement Senghor) jouant au wouré surplombent l’emblématique casque de samouraï, qui côtoie à son tour les armoiries de la marine japonaise. Un de ses bateaux, à la dernière escale à Dakar, a déposé les nouveaux sceaux. Au tout dernier niveau, une magnifique plaquette en bois signée l’artiste Mbaye Diop a sous ses pieds une défense d’éléphant sculptée de figures anthropomorphes et zoomorphes et le médaillon du duc de Lévis Mirepoix. Toujours au rez-de-chaussée, une tapisserie de Papa Ibra Tall agrémente la salle de réception, comme pour prolonger la symbolique de la Salle des Banquets. Juste au-dessus de cette œuvre exceptionnelle, la sculpture que Senghor plaçait à côté de lui durant ses adresses à la nation résiste au temps et à ses érosions. La lumière permanente de cet espace est offerte par un bassin encerclé de vitres et dégagé vers le ciel, pour la joie de Senghor qui voulait couler sa retraite paisiblement. Au-delà du faste, l’installation donne de la fraîcheur au travail de décoration de Jean-Pierre Brossard. Leurs âmes y séjournent encore… La piscine décorative brillait aussi les yeux des invités du Salon blanc, où recevait Mme Senghor, et du Salon rose, salle d’attente pour le bureau de M. Senghor. Ce bureau est maintenant occupé par Mme Marième Ndoye, conservatrice du Musée Léopold Sédar Senghor. Au Salon vert, dans le séjour privé, on sent la féminité et l’allure distinguée de Mme Colette Senghor. La couleur est de son désir, d’ailleurs, elle, la Normande qui ne peut vivre sans verdure autour. C’est ainsi que le vert domine la pièce, barrée par une vitre qui relate une part d’amour du couple. Un poème de Senghor y est affiché, depuis la 15e Biennale de l’art africain contemporain. Ça dit : « Or Sénégalaise aux Sénégalaises s’était voulue la Normande de long lignage, aux yeux de moire vert et or ». Ah, qu’il est fleur bleue, ce bon vieux Sédar. Mais sa « Blonde d’amour » le lui rendait bien. Par la cuisine en art de la bonne chère, par sa loyauté, son dévouement et son regard sur la ligne. Tenez, c’est écrit à la main par Mme Senghor « Ascenseur en panne » sur la porte de l’élévateur pour contraindre Léopold à monter les marches et faire de l’exercice. Un couloir mène ensuite aux deux chambres d’amis. Dans la première, on y garde encore le berceau de Philippe Senghor et des robes de créateur de Mme Colette Senghor. Ces empreintes font survivre les âmes des anciens occupants de la maison, surtout quand doivent surgir les marques de tragédie. Par Mamadou Oumar KAMARA

items.title: Samini explains why he avoids X Spaces, TikTok Live sessions
items.description: Ghanaian dancehall musician Samini says he avoids X Spaces and TikTok Live sessions because they can expose him to disrespect and damage his carefully built brand. The award-winning artiste made this known at the launch of the Samini Xperience 2026, Dansoman Edition, on Friday, 16th October 2026, as he prepares to bring his signature concert to Dansoman during the festive season. Samini explained that although people and businesses must adapt to changing trends, not every new approach to communication is necessarily prudent. “There are always new ways of doing things and we always adapt but you see, not all those ways are prudent,” he said. He recalled a time before social media when fans had fewer opportunities to interact directly with established musicians, explaining that they often had to attend concerts to see their favourite artistes. “Before social media. Before you could tweet at me and say ‘your mother’, the only place you would see me was when they had booked me for show and you have bought your ticket to be in that show and there is a standby photographer that you were hoping to take me and you so that you can say you have been able to [get close to me],” he added. According to Samini, the rise of social media has made it easier for people to approach celebrities online and make comments they might not have made in person. “So for things like Twitter Spaces and TikTok Live, you are live, and some boy in some corner now has the opportunity to say whatever they want to you. And they go overboard to say things to you that if you are not careful as a human being you get derailed and you say things that eventually gonna go detrimental to your hard built brand. So if you have not seen me in those places, these are the reasons,” he noted. He said such interactions could provoke artistes into responding in ways that might ultimately harm their public image and professional reputation. Samini, however, clarified that he had not completely ruled out participating in X Spaces or TikTok Live sessions. He said he could consider joining such discussions if he believed they would contribute to his craft and serve a meaningful professional purpose. The celebrated musician added that his team would carefully assess potential engagements and select participants who could add value to discussions and contribute positively to the projects or initiatives involved.

items.title: L’investissement allemand crée de l’emploi et booste l’économie locale
items.description: A l’image de GAUFF ENGINEERING et de Klingele Paper & Packaging des entreprises allemandes présentes au Sénégal forment des compétences et créent les conditions d’un emploi durable. Le partenariat économique entre l’Allemagne et le Sénégal ne se lit pas seulement dans les montants investis. Il se mesure aussi dans les infrastructures qui rapprochent les territoires, les usines qui transforment localement les produits, les compétences qui se transmettent et les emplois qui se créent. Sur le terrain, plusieurs entreprises allemandes ont choisi de s’inscrire dans cette dynamique, en adaptant leur savoir-faire aux besoins du marché sénégalais. Klingele Paper & Packaging et GAUFF ENGINEERING en donnent une illustration concrète. La première s’installe au cœur de la nouvelle géographie industrielle de Diamniadio. La seconde intervient dans l’électrification rurale, avec une nouvelle phase qui doit étendre son action à des centaines de villages. « On a considéré que le Sénégal était la porte de la CEDEAO », explique Guillermo Rodríguez, directeur régional Afrique de l’Ouest de l’entreprise. Cette implantation a également révélé à Klingele un autre atout du Sénégal : ses ressources humaines. L’expérience mauritanienne avait imposé au groupe un effort de formation interne important. « La différence entre les deux pays ne tient pas aux hommes, elle tient à l’écosystème de formation. En Mauritanie, nous avons dû construire nos compétences en interne, et les équipes de Nouadhibou et de Nouakchott en sont aujourd’hui la meilleure preuve. Au Sénégal, nous avons trouvé un réseau d’écoles de formation professionnelle déjà très dense, ce qui a considérablement allégé notre investissement en formation initiale et nous a permis de monter en puissance plus vite. ». L’entreprise recrute localement, envoie certains collaborateurs se former dans ses usines en Allemagne et fait intervenir des techniciens sur place. « 100 % de notre personnel, des trois usines que nous avons sur le continent africain, est local », se réjouit le directeur régional. Le groupe familial allemand, fondé en 1920, possède aujourd’hui 21 usines de cartons ondulés dans douze pays. Au Sénégal, Klingele a acquis, en 2023, 24 000 m² dans le pôle industriel de Diamniadio. Le projet a bénéficié d’un financement de 5 millions d’euros avec l’appui de la KfW-DEG, tandis que la GIZ a accompagné l’entreprise sur le volet de la formation. L’objectif, selon le directeur régional, est d’atteindre progressivement 100 à 120 emplois, contre 26 actuellement. Ce développement accompagne directement les besoins des filières agricoles. L’emballage n’est pas ici un simple produit fini. Il constitue un maillon de la chaîne qui permet de protéger, transporter et valoriser les productions sénégalaises destinées aux marchés internationaux. GAUFF ENGINEERING, électrifier pour libérer l’activité économique Après Diamniadio, l’investissement allemand prend une autre forme. Avec GAUFF ENGINEERING, il passe par les réseaux électriques, les centrales photovoltaïques et les infrastructures qui doivent rapprocher l’énergie des populations rurales. GAUFF a assuré en tant que Maître d’Œuvre les études, les préparations des appels d’offres, la supervision des exécutions et la gestion du projet. La première phase du projet nommé « ASER-300-villages » mené avec le Maître d’Ouvrage l’Agence Sénégalaise d’Electrification Rurale (ASER), de 2019 à 2025, avait permis de contribuer à l’électrification de 372 villages, selon Lutz Ekhoff, le directeur du projet de GAUFF ENGINEERING à Dakar, dans un entretien accordé au journal Le Soleil. Le programme comprenait en plus 90 sites destinés à des activités génératrices de revenus (AGR) : périmètres maraîchers, chambres froides, machines à glace et plateformes post-récolte. Environ 860 jeunes Sénégalais et des opérateurs/ concessionnaires avaient parallèlement été formés dans le domaine de l’électrification et sa gestion. Le financement de cette première phase avait été assuré par la KfW IPEX-Bank à hauteur de 120 millions d’euros. Ces chiffres, qui ont touchés autour de 200.000 personnes au milieu rurale, racontent une transformation qui dépasse le simple raccordement des foyer privés. À noter au-delà que dans les sites électrifiés, l’énergie peut servir à pomper l’eau, conserver une production ou faire fonctionner une machine. « Avoir l’électricité peut même quelquefois permettre d’approvisionner les pompes dans les puits ou les machines sur les plateformes post-agricole », explique M. Ekhoff. De plus pour les productions agricoles et halieutiques, l’enjeu est également celui de la conservation. « Il est désormais possible d’avoir des frigos et des chambres froides, que nous avons notamment développé pour stocker les productions agricoles et d’élevage, ainsi que de créer un certain nombre de machines à glace pour les conservations des pêcheurs », poursuit-il. Une deuxième phase de l’électrification rurale – tournée vers le sud et le sud-est du Sénégal GAUFF ENGINEERING prépare désormais une nouvelle étape de son intervention avec l’ASER. A en croire le directeur, la nouvelle deuxième phase du programme devrait concerner 750 villages, avec une concentration importante dans le sud et le sud-est du Sénégal. La majorité des localités concernées devrait être raccordée au réseau existant de moyenne tension et d’autre 180 villages devraient être équipés de centrales photovoltaïques et des mini-réseaux. Le démarrage est espéré en 2027. Le volume financier envisagé est à nouveau d’environ 120 millions d’euros, soit un niveau comparable à celui de la première phase. Cette nouvelle étape prolonge donc une approche dans laquelle l’infrastructure est pensée avec son effet sur l’économie locale. Former des jeunes, alimenter des équipements hydrauliques, permettre la conservation des produits ou soutenir des activités génératrices de revenus : l’électricité devient un levier de développement. Klingele et GAUFF misent sur le Sénégal comme espace de production. Ils créent ou préparent des emplois. Ils transmettent des compétences. Ils s’appuient sur des partenaires sénégalais. Et ils bénéficient, chacun dans son domaine, de l’écosystème de la coopération allemande, à travers notamment la KfW/DEG et la GIZ. Par Adama NDIAYE et Babacar Guèye DIOP

items.title: One in three adults in Pakistan lives with psychological disorder: study
items.description: KARACHI: Pakistan’s first nationally representative mental health survey has shown that nearly one in three adults is living with a diagnosable mental and behavioural disorder, highlighting a major public health challenge affecting millions of people across the country. The findings come from the largest and most comprehensive mental health study ever conducted in Pakistan, say researchers representing the Pakistan Psychiatric Society (PPS). The five-year research is published in the British Medical Journal . The survey was led by Professor Raza-ur-Rahman from Hamdard University, Karachi, in collaboration with Brighton and Sussex Medical School UK, University of South Florida, US, and psychiatric institutions across Pakistan. Experts term findings of first national mental health survey ‘most reliable’ Nearly 18,000 adults from all four provinces participated in the 2018-2022 study, providing the first nationally representative picture of mental health in the country. Key findings The study found that 32 per cent of adults were currently living with mental and behavioural disorders, while 38 per cent had experienced a disorder during their lifetime. One in five adults met criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). More than one in 10 adults had depression, whereas six per cent reported suicidal thoughts in the previous month. Researchers also identified significant social inequalities in mental health. Higher rates of mental disorders were found among older adults, individuals with lower levels of education and income, unemployed people, and those who were widowed, divorced or separated. Mental health problems were associated with substantial impairment in family life, social relationships and the ability to work. “This survey provides the evidence needed to develop effective mental health policies and services in Pakistan. It identifies who is most at risk, where support is most needed, and the scale of the unmet need for care,” said lead investigator Prof Raza-ur-Rahman, currently heading the department of psychiatry at HU. According to him, the researchers used international standard tools to carry out the survey and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics identified the areas for survey and provided the sample size. He hoped that it would contribute to reducing stigma and improving access to diagnosis and treatment for millions of people. “For the first time, policymakers, healthcare planners and researchers now have reliable national data that can be used to strengthen mental health services, allocate resources more effectively and develop evidence-based programmes across the country,” he added. The study represents a major milestone for mental health research in Pakistan and demonstrates the country’s growing capacity to undertake large-scale, internationally recognised public health research. Prof Anjum Memon, Chair in Epidemiology and Public Health Medicine at Brighton and Sussex Medical School (UK) and the senior co-author of the study, said: “This is a landmark moment for mental health research in Pakistan. For decades, policymakers have had to rely on fragmented local studies or international estimates. We now have robust national evidence showing, for the first time, the true scale of mental and behavioural disorders across the country.” These findings provide an invaluable evidence base for policymakers, clinicians and healthcare planners, not only in Pakistan but also in other low- and middle-income countries facing similar challenges, he added. Mental health, researchers say, is increasingly recognised as an essential component of national health and economic development and they recommend greater integration of mental health services into primary healthcare, increased investment in community-based support systems, enhanced training for frontline health workers and sustained national efforts to reduce the stigma surrounding mental illness. “Pakistan currently faces major challenges in the provision of mental healthcare, including limited specialist services and a shortage of trained mental health professionals. The survey findings will help inform future policy development, service planning, workforce training and community-based support programmes,” said President of PPS Prof Wajid Akhundzada. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: 2027: Why I’m best man for Ogun job —Yayi
items.description: •Cites 24 years’ legislative experience, accountancy background •Unveils nine-point agenda, promises jobs, industrialisation, better roads •Says Yewa-Awori deserves governorship after 50 years •Speaks on Ekiti origin claim By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, has made a case for his suitability to govern Ogun State in 2027, citing 24 years of legislative experience, his professional background as an accountant and his commitment to consolidate the achievements of Governor Dapo Abiodun. The All Progressives Congress, APC, governorship candidate, who unveiled his nine-point development blueprint, the ITESIWAJU Agenda, recently, in an interview with journalists in Lagos, said his ambition was driven by a passion to serve the people and transform the state, rather than personal enrichment. Adeola, who is seeking to become governor on his third attempt to return to Ogun politics, after 20 years sojourn in Lagos, also argued that the Yewa-Awori axis deserved to produce the state’s next governor, having yet to occupy the position in the state’s 50-year history. He described the 2027 election as an opportunity to sustain the foundation he said Abiodun had laid for economic growth, industrialisation and improved public services. “My ambition to be the governor of this state is not based on personal interest or plan to enrich myself or to be in that exalted office to be called governor, but based on passion to serve. Passion to serve the people of Ogun,” he said. Why I’m qualified Adeola, 57, said his experience across the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate had equipped him with the legislative, financial and administrative knowledge required to govern Ogun. A chartered accountant, he spent 13 years at The Guardian newspapers before entering elective politics. He was elected to represent Alimosho in the Lagos State House of Assembly in 2002, serving for eight years before moving to the House of Representatives. He subsequently represented Lagos West Senatorial District for eight years before moving to Ogun West, which he currently represents in the Senate. The lawmaker said the experience had given him an understanding of public finance, lawmaking and the policy choices necessary to move Ogun forward. He maintained that the state needed a leader who could build on existing achievements while translating economic opportunities into jobs, infrastructure and improved living standards. “I strongly feel that the next person in line must come to consolidate on the gains we have made in the last seven and a half years as a state,” he said. Why Yewa-Awori should produce governor Adeola identified the long-standing absence of a governor from the Yewa-Awori axis as another consideration in the 2027 contest. The Ilaro-born politician argued that the area’s claim should be considered alongside the need for competent leadership and inclusive development. “If elected, it will be the first time somebody from the Yewa-Awori axis will become governor,” he said, making regional representation a key part of his appeal to voters. He, however, presented his candidacy primarily as a vehicle for economic transformation, insisting that Ogun had the natural resources, industrial base and strategic location to become Nigeria’s biggest economy. Nine-point Itesiwaju Agenda Adeola said his ITESIWAJU Agenda, built around the motto, “Nine priorities. One vision. One Ogun,” would focus on infrastructure, industrialisation, agriculture, education, healthcare, security, youth and women’s empowerment, tourism, environmental sustainability and improved fiscal management. A central objective, he said, would be to position Ogun as a self-sustaining industrial hub capable of generating employment and reducing the movement of skilled workers to neighbouring Lagos State. On infrastructure, he promised major road rehabilitation, including the Mowe-Ofada axis, alongside mass transit bus services and commuter rail connections between Abeokuta and Lagos. He promised to do inner roads and ensure demolition of buildings was not the first option at OPIC lands at Ilutuntun, Agbara and other areas. The senator pledged to strengthen agriculture and food security through diversification, improve educational standards and human capital development, and expand access to healthcare. Security would involve closer collaboration with community-based structures, including the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, while youth and women’s empowerment programmes would provide opportunities for economic participation. He proposed cooperative arrangements for commercial drivers, including car, tricycle and motorcycle operators, with access to health insurance and vehicle financing. Tourism and the creative arts would also feature in his economic plans, alongside urban renewal, environmental sustainability, physical planning, public finance reforms and improved local administration. Deep seaport, dairy farm, minerals Beyond the manifesto, Adeola pointed to what he described as the economic foundations laid by the Abiodun administration, arguing that the state’s development should be assessed not only by visible infrastructure but also by projects expected to generate future prosperity. He cited a proposed N7 billion deep seaport, for which he said groundbreaking was expected in November, as well as a dairy farm with an initial 500 cattle and a target of 15,000 cattle within two years. He also mentioned a major furniture-making company and plans for crude oil exploitation at Tongeji Island, which he said had 12 basins. “Governor Abiodun has laid a very solid foundation. It is for me to consolidate and ensure all these come to pass,” he said. Adeola said Ogun’s natural resources offered substantial opportunities for investment, industrial growth and employment if properly managed. He pledged to pursue licences for mineral exploration and mining, while ensuring that local communities and the state benefited from the exploitation of their resources. “I will domesticate Local Content Act in Ogun State. We (National Assembly) have expanded the scope of the Act to cover every sector instead of oil. In exploring mineral resources, Ogun will not be a dumping ground under my watch but a partner. I will apply competitively and bid for minerals mining licences in Ogun for companies to come and partner with us,” he said. His proposed approach, he added, would seek to attract investors while ensuring that Ogun was not reduced to a mere supplier of raw materials or a dumping ground for mining-related activities. Healthcare, sports, wealth creation On healthcare, Adeola promised to sustain Abiodun’s free healthcare programme for residents aged 65 and above and build 20 hospitals, each in a four-storey building, across the state’s 20 local government areas. He also pledged to revive sports, citing the state’s large youth population, which he said accounted for about 65 per cent of its population. A new Ministry of Wealth Creation, he said, would provide an institutional framework for continuing his annual empowerment programmes and expanding opportunities for residents. The proposed programmes, he argued, would complement industrialisation and infrastructure development by enabling more people to participate in the state’s economy. 10% of revenue for councils Adeola also backed financial autonomy for local governments, promising to set aside 10 per cent of the state’s revenue for allocation to the councils. He said stronger local administrations would bring governance closer to residents and reduce the burden on the state government. “Effective LGAs will ensure less stress for the state because they will take care of a lot of things,” he said. The proposal, if implemented, would make local councils important partners in delivering basic services and addressing community-level development needs. Third attempt, Abiodun’s backing His bid to return to Ogun politics, he said, had encountered resistance during the administration of former Governor Ibikunle Amosun, forcing him to return to Lagos politics. He said his third attempt in 2023 succeeded with the support of Abiodun, who is now backing his governorship ambition. “2023 was my third attempt to return to Ogun State to continue my political activities. God used Governor Dapo Abiodun to make it possible,” he said. Adeola said his emergence as the APC governorship candidate placed him in a position to sustain the current administration’s policies and projects. He maintained that Ogun had performed well under Abiodun, arguing that development involved both ‘seen’ projects, such as roads, schools and hospitals, and ‘unseen’ economic foundations that could deliver long-term prosperity. He said his responsibility, if elected, would be to ensure that ongoing initiatives translated into tangible benefits for residents. Ekiti origin claims are political gimmicks The APC candidate also dismissed claims that he was from Ekiti State, insisting that both sides of his family originated from Ogun. “My father is from Ogun State, my mother is from Ogun State. I am from Ogun State. Those who claim I am from Ekiti are jesters,” he said. He equally rejected claims that his late father was buried in Ekiti, saying he was buried at the house he built on Ogunsola Street, Alaguntan, in Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos. “My father was not buried in Ekiti; my father was buried in the house he built at Ogunsola Street at Alaguntan in Alimosho,” he said. Adeola described the claims as political tactics that would not succeed. “They are just playing politics with ridiculous claims, and they will not succeed,” he added. Vanguard News The post 2027: Why I’m best man for Ogun job —Yayi appeared first on Vanguard News .
