items.title: D Cryme calls for museum, podcast studio to honour Dr Duncan
items.description: Ghanaian musician D Cryme has called on music industry stakeholders to celebrate broadcaster Dr Duncan for his role in projecting several musicians through his Kasahare Level show on Adom FM in the 2000s. Speaking to arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie on Joy FM’s Showbiz A-Z , D Cryme outlined several ways the industry could honour Dr Duncan for his contribution to music. “Dr Duncan does not only deserve a statue, but he deserves a super big monumented museum. While he is alive, he deserves all the accolades and appreciation. That is why I mention him wherever I go,” he said. D Cryme said musicians who benefited from the platform Dr Duncan provided should not wait until his death before speaking about his impact on their careers and the music industry. “This is what I want to see him do; if things come and it’s proper, I would rather create a nice podcast for him. Podcast is the way. He still has something in him. It’s just like a solid young but grandpa in the house,” he added. He also noted that others who shared his vision could join forces with him to make the proposed project a reality. “It’s something that I tell my friends and industry colleagues. It’s something I have been trumpeting. I try to let them know that maybe I might have the means but it is not one man fight or one man projection. That clearly tells you that you also have equally something extra to spare. We can pull our resources together. We can make this happen,” D Cryme said. Dr Duncan’s Kasahare Level on Adom FM became a platform for aspiring musicians, particularly rappers, to showcase their lyrical skills and gain exposure in the Ghanaian music industry during the 2000s. The programme helped bring emerging talents before a wider audience at a time when radio airplay was an important route to recognition. Several musicians have been associated with the programme’s influence, including D Cryme and other artistes who built their profiles through radio exposure and the hiplife scene. The programme served as a launchpad for artistes such as Sarkodie, Yaa Pono, Pope Skinny, Shakoma, Stonebwoy, D Cryme, Criss Waddle, Yaw Siki, Edem, Guru, Kwaw Kese, Kofi Korea, and others, several of whom later established themselves in Ghana’s music industry.

items.title: Trump paused Russia sanctions to 'analyse' impact on global economy: Rubio
items.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump’s waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to “analyse” their impact on the global economy. “The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy,” Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Houthis. “These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they’re having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices” but on economies as well, Rubio said. Trump said late on Saturday his decision would benefit the US, though it was unclear if he had actually made up his mind on the matter. “We’ll figure it out, and you’ll figure it out,” he said. “It’s a very good decision, and it’s going to be a decision that’s good for the country, and I think good for the world.” US lawmakers on both sides of the political aisle have sharply criticised Trump after he signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia — measures adopted by Congress last month. The law passed in September, and signed by Trump, included sanctions targeting Russian officials, oligarchs and financial institutions, and provided Trump with the authority to impose sanctions on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The idea was to cut off sources of funding to supporters of Russian President Vladimir Putin, as well as his war on Ukraine. But late Friday, two days before the law was due to take effect, Trump exempted Russia from those economic restrictions. “Beyond irresponsible,” Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a frequent Trump critic who will leave office in January, said in a post on X. “If the President wants to actually bring down energy prices, he can do it by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid for Vladimir Putin.” Ted Cruz, a senior Republican senator from Texas, called the move “a mistake” in comments aired on Fox News . Trump’s executive order came after he struck a deal with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin to allow exports of Russian diesel in exchange for the easing of sanctions. The impact of steep diesel price hikes due to the Iran war are beginning to filter into the US economy, and cost of living worries are top of mind for voters ahead of key midterm elections next month. Polls show Trump’s Republicans are likely to receive a drubbing at the polls. “The diesel that Putin was going to sell, they were (going to) make it available to the global market one way or the other. The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get,” Rubio said, underscoring the importance of the vital fuel powering US road hauling, agriculture and construction. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said he feared the United States would lift more sanctions on Russia and that Trump’s action “rewards” Putin.

items.title: Somalie: le calendrier pour les élections générales est déjà contesté
items.description: La Somalie connait enfin le calendrier de ses futures élections générales. Les législatives se tiendront en avril 2027 et la présidentielle en mai. La Commission électorale nationale indépendante l’a annoncé le jeudi 15 octobre. Ces scrutins devaient avoir lieu cette année. Mais ils ont été repoussés, à la faveur d’une réforme électorale qui doit instaurer le système de suffrage universel, volonté forte du président sortant, Hassan Cheikh Mohamoud. C’est la première fois depuis 1969, que les Somaliens voteront selon le principe : une personne, un vote. Mais cette réforme et le nouveau calendrier sont déjà vivement contestés.

items.title: Joyce Bawah Mogtari shares O-Level setback and success story at Assisi Girls SHS anniversary
items.description: Joyce Bawah Mogtari arrived at St Francis of Assisi Girls’ Senior High School in Jirapa to resit her O-Level examinations after an unsuccessful attempt. The school gave her a second chance. Today, she returned as a senior lawyer, Senior Presidential Advisor and Special Aide to President John Dramani Mahama. Her return as Special Guest of Honour for the school’s 67th anniversary and FOGA Homecoming was also the homecoming of a daughter who found her path in Jirapa. Delivering the keynote address on Saturday, October 17, on the theme, “67 Years of Nurturing Leaders and Inspiring Excellence: Time to Retrace Our Steps”, she shared an emotional account of how she came to Assisi. “There is something profoundly satisfying about returning to a place that once offered you your dreams,” she began. “I came here to resit my O-Levels because it was an exam that literally eluded me.” Her uncle, who had been transferred to Wa as the Inspector-General of Police’s representative, recommended Assisi as “quiet and just the kind of place that I needed”. “The rest, as they say, is history,” she said. The records, she said, would show that she obtained a distinction and won WAEC awards for Best Student in English Language and Home Economics. “Let me tell you something else, the Home Economics and typing – not French and Maths – gave me the best possible results,” she said to cheers. She paid tribute to the then headmistress, Mrs Gyader, and Madam Dakurah, a former student of her mother. “The sense of Catholicism I developed came from here – my independence and spirit of competition was likewise borne from here. Some of the best friends that I have I met them here too. And finally the man I eventually married also hails from this region. They say that the best comes from the West.” Reflecting on her journey, she asked: “Who would have imagined, all those years ago, that one day I would return to this school as a very Senior Lawyer, Maritime Lawyer, founder of a Law Firm, an entrepreneur and Senior Presidential Advisor and Special Aide to the President?” Mahama’s message Mrs Mogtari also conveyed President Mahama’s greetings to the school community. “I bring you greetings and warm wishes from the President. His Excellency remains deeply committed to expanding educational opportunities for all Ghanaians, particularly girls and young women,” she said. “The President recognises that when we invest in the education of girls, we invest not only in their individual futures, but also in the prosperity and progress of our nation.” ‘Marry your books’ To the current students, she offered a clear piece of advice: “Marry your books!” “For now, let your textbooks be your closest companions. Let your assignments command your attention,” she said. “Do not spend so much time on social media that you neglect your studies. Failure in one examination is not failure in life.” Citing Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang’s achievement as Ghana’s first female Vice-President, she said the next barrier to overcome was electing a female President. “Perhaps she is sitting in a classroom somewhere in Ghana today. Perhaps she is sitting right here at St. Francis of Assisi Girls’ Senior High School. Why should that not be possible?” She praised President Mahama for choosing Prof Opoku-Agyemang as his running mate in the 2020 and 2024 elections. Acta Non Verba – deeds, not words The presidential aide, who often signs off on Facebook with the phrase Acta Non Verba , joked about its similarity to Holy Child School’s motto, Facta Non Verba . “I did not attend Holy Child. Neither did I borrow my personal creed from the school,” she said with a laugh. “Acta Non Verba reflects something I believe very strongly. Our words must be supported by our actions.” She challenged the old students to reflect on the opportunities the school had given them and how they could improve the experience for the next generation. “What opportunities did this school give us? What are we prepared to do to make the experience even better?” she asked. “The measure of our gratitude is not simply how proudly we speak about St. Francis. It is what we are prepared to do for St. Francis.” She urged FOGA to ensure that “every homecoming leaves behind more than photographs and pleasant memories”. Her final charge to the students was: “Dream boldly. Study diligently. Conduct yourselves with integrity.”

items.title: Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair draws patrons with discounts of up to 30% as event enters final day in Ho
items.description: Exhibitors at the Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair in Ho are offering discounts of up to 30% on selected products and services as the event enters its final day. JoyNews reporter Maxwell Agbagba, reporting from the Ho Sports Stadium, says the offers are attracting prospective homeowners and other patrons seeking affordable housing solutions. The discounts have added to activity at the venue, where exhibitors are showcasing products and services covering various aspects of homeownership, construction and property development. The offerings range from building materials and home appliances to real estate financing options and property development services. Patrons have also expressed satisfaction with the range of housing and real estate solutions available at the fair. The fair remains open until 8 p.m. today, giving visitors a final opportunity to explore the available offers, compare products and engage directly with exhibitors. The Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair brings together businesses and other stakeholders in Ghana’s housing and real estate sector, connecting consumers with products, services and information to support their homeownership plans. This year’s edition in Ho forms part of efforts to extend the fair’s reach beyond Accra and other major urban centres, bringing housing-related products and services closer to prospective buyers in the Volta Region and surrounding areas. Organised by JoyNews and sponsored by Republic Bank, the event provides a platform for exhibitors to engage potential customers while allowing patrons to explore available options in the housing market. With the fair closing at 8 p.m., interested patrons have until this evening to visit the Ho Sports Stadium and take advantage of the offers available.

items.title: Broken record: Contested boundaries, founding challenges and a provincial govt dismissed
items.description: The issues of Dawn of Aug 18 till Aug 24, 1947 were dominated by the announcement of the Radcliffe Commission award, setting the formal boundaries of the dominions of Pakistan and India, while communal violence, and efforts to quell it on both sides, also featured prominently on the pages. In more welcome news, the bureaucracy in the nascent state rolled up their sleeves to take up the task of nation-building — which remains a work in progress, mind you — while congratulations continued to pour in welcoming Pakistan to the comity of nations. In the Aug 18 edition, the reaction in the lead story to the announcement of the Radcliffe Commission award was highly critical. “The decisions embodied in the reports very materially alter the boundaries as set forth provisionally under the national division and it is the Indian Union which gains all along the line at the expense of Pakistan.” In a related report, Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, the Communication Minister, acerbically termed it “a parting kick of the British”. Clearly, the founding fathers felt His Majesty’s government had pulled a fast one on Pakistan. Apparently, they were not wrong. Aug 18’s lead editorial termed Sir Cyril Radcliffe’s decision “Territorial Murder”. As the editorial noted, the decision had come like a “bolt from the blue. They represent the award of only one man, Sir Cyril Radcliffe, the Chairman [of the commission]. … The Muslim nation has been betrayed. … Pakistan has been cheated of large areas in the Punjab, Bengal and the district of Sylhet which … belonged to it.” This was, in the words of the Quaid-i-Azam, a “moth-eaten Pakistan”. Punjab disturbances Communal bloodshed, particularly in Punjab, remained a major concern for both Pakistan and India. As the lead story on Aug 19 noted, there were “widespread massacres in the Eastern Punjab, particularly in the Amritsar district.” So serious were matters that Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan, and his Indian counterpart Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru were briefed on the security situation by Sir Claude Auchinleck, who was supreme commander of both dominions at the time. The Quaid was also informed of the situation by the PM. Taking care of business, UN application But even in the midst of grave challenges, there was much work to be done. As the joy of living in a newly independent nation began to sink in, so did the gravity of the task of governing it. Aug 19 was the first working day of the Pakistan government. The Aug 20 edition noted that “about 5,000 Officers, typists and assistants, turned up for work. All the files have not yet arrived from Delhi.” It added that “every means of conveyance was used” by the public servants of the new state to show up for duty; even “camel carts were not considered too undignified”. Can you imagine today’s babus showing up for work in carts drawn by animals, or even worse, using public transport like the rest of us plebeians? Perish the thought. Nothing but the slickest, most expensive wheels for today’s ‘servants’ of the people. Meanwhile, as the Aug 18 issue reported, Pakistan submitted its application to the United Nations. “The formal letter of application arrived from Karachi at United Nations Headquarters today [Aug 16]. Interestingly, the UN Legal Department had decided that while the “new Dominion of India would continue to be an original member state” of the UN, “Pakistan, as a new State, would have to apply for membership.” Thankfully, Pakistan’s application was accepted in September 1947, with Afghanistan casting the sole vote against this country’s membership. Pakistan greeted In the days after independence, numerous heads of state wrote to the Quaid congratulating Pakistan on its birth. For example US President Harry S. Truman assured Pakistan of the “firm friendship and goodwill of the USA.” French Foreign Minister Georges Bidault described the raising of Pakistan “to the rank of the great free nations as a step of great importance for the whole world.” Al-Haj Amin al-Husseini, Grand Mufti of Jerusalem (which had not yet been occupied by Israel) offered the “most sincere congratulations of your Palestinian brethren and their best wishes.” Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia, took “great pleasure in extending our greetings” to Pakistan while the Iranian Prime Minister Ahmad Qavam said: “May Pakistan become a great bulwark of freedom, peace and brotherhood in Asia”. Clearly, nations of the East and West had great expectations of Pakistan. Dr Khan Sahib’s ministry The Aug 23 issue contained a news item many current readers will find quite interesting, to say the least. As per a communique issued from Governor House Peshawar on Aug 22, “Dr Khan Sahib’s Ministry has today [Aug 22] been dismissed from office and the Governor has invited Khan Abdul Qayum Khan, Leader of the Opposition Muslim League Party in the NWFP Legislative Assembly to form a Ministry”. Dr Khan Sahib was the brother of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the “Frontier Gandhi”, who famously did not see eye to eye with Pakistan’s founding fathers. Dr Khan Sahib’s Congress Ministry had taken office in March 1946, and had faced a civil disobedience movement. An elected government in the NWFP (now KP) led by an opposition party was sent home by the centre at the birth of Pakistan. Sound familiar? With the advantage of hindsight, one has the opportunity to study the historical cycles in a nation’s life. Thanks to this newspaper’s unique, extensive archive of back issues, one can examine the major political, economic and social trends that have shaped Pakistan and the world over the last seven decades and counting. Cliched as it may sound, history repeats itself, and we — as a state and as a polity — largely refuse to learn from it. Through this platform, we will look back at the ‘big’ stories that made it to the front pages of Dawn, as well as significant developments tucked away in the inside pages, from the birth of Pakistan onwards, and try to put them in perspective. We will study the critical issues of the week, starting from Aug 14, 1947 and examine the major themes and issues that made it to the paper.

items.title: Samuel Jinapor questions expected economic benefits of Ghana’s proposed BRICS partnership
items.description: The Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has questioned the benefits outlined by the government for Ghana’s proposed partnership with BRICS, describing the expectations as unrealistic. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 17, 2026, the Damongo MP argued that Ghana would still require clearance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to access certain forms of financial assistance. In his view, this would limit the opportunities Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa had suggested the partnership would offer. “It is comforting that we have been told now, that we are not going for full membership, but that we are starting with partnership. That is all well and good, but the point we (the minority in parliament) made, which I want to reiterate, is that in taking this decision- in other words, making a move to join BRICS, to join G20, even the New Development Bank- the point is that for you to access funding from the New Development Bank, you need IMF approval, and so the argument that this is going to help us move away from the dollar, that this is going to help us broaden our opportunities and to stabilise our currency, I am afraid, is a bit simplistic because you need IMF approval,” he said. Mr Jinapor nevertheless welcomed the government’s decision to pursue the relationship, acknowledging that initial steps towards engagement with BRICS began under the administration of former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. He said it was positive that the current administration was continuing that process, but maintained that the anticipated benefits needed to be assessed realistically. His comments followed Mr Ablakwa’s explanation that Ghana was seeking partner status with BRICS rather than full membership, as part of efforts to broaden its international cooperation.

items.title: ONP : baisse de 14% des débarquements de pêche au port d'Al Hoceima
items.description: L’Office national des pêches (ONP), a fait état d’une baisse de 14% des débarquements des produits de la pêche côtière et artisanale au port d’Al Hoceima à fin septembre 2026, pour s’établir à 1.655 tonnes. Dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques de la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc, l’ONP précise que la valeur marchande de ces captures a également reculé de 17% pour s'établir à environ 90,64 millions de dirhams (MDH), contre plus de 109,01 MDH à fin septembre 2025. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont régressé de 23% à 243 T, pour une valeur estimée à plus de 10,16 MDH (-17%), contre plus de 12,29 MDH/315 T à fin septembre 2025. Les débarquements des poissons blancs ont augmenté de 10% à 266 T à fin septembre dernier, pour une valeur de plus de 11,20 MDH, contre environ 9,48 MDH à fin septembre 2025, soit une hausse de 18% en glissement annuel. Concernant les débarquement des céphalopodes, ils ont baissé de 18% atteignant 1.066 T pour des recettes d'environ 63,44 MDH (-22%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont évolué de 29% à 80 T, générant des revenus de plus de 5,83 MDH (+8%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à 965.832 T à fin septembre dernier, en hausse de 19% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 6% à plus de 8,68 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre environ 8,20 MMDH en glissement annuel. The post ONP : baisse de 14% des débarquements de pêche au port d'Al Hoceima appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: IN CASE OF EMERGENCY
items.description: Last week, the government of Pakistan imposed emergency rule and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). The Pashtun-majority province, which shares a long border with Afghanistan, has been deeply shaped by events across the frontier. KP’s instability escalated during the 1980s, when Gen Ziaul Haq’s dictatorship, backed by American and Saudi funding, transformed Pakistan into a launching pad for anti-Soviet Afghan Islamist insurgents. After the Soviet withdrawal in 1988, Pakistan aligned with the Afghan Taliban (TTA), who took power in Kabul in 1996. Even after the US forces ousted the TTA in 2001, Pakistan provided TTA fighters sanctuary to counter the new regime in Kabul installed by the US. In 2007, the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) emerged. While the TTA maintained ties with Pakistan’s security establishment, they also cultivated ideological links with the TTP. However, the TTA remained passive as the TTP carried out brutal attacks inside Pakistan. Despite a major Pakistani military offensive (2015–2017) that displaced the TTP, Pakistan maintained the belief that the TTA were ‘good Taliban’ who would remain allies once in power. TTP became the ‘bad Taliban.’ The strategy was as juvenile as it sounds. Under the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), the government began resettling TTP fighters who had escaped to Afghanistan. There was no serious bar on them retaining their weapons and regrouping. This was yet another juvenile move by the state and its then-favourite government. Decades of contradictory policies towards the Afghan and Pakistani Taliban have left Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mired in insecurity. As the state imposes emergency rule in KP, the question is whether extraordinary powers can help correct the state’s longstanding strategic failures Understandably, during the TTA’s return to power in 2021 in Afghanistan and Imran Khan’s ouster in 2022, the TTP launched a fresh wave of violent attacks, primarily in KP. The TTP had sensed that, after Khan’s fall, the policy of the new military establishment might shift. And it did. Today, the federal government and military establishment accuse KP’s PTI-led provincial administration of shielding TTP elements. Meanwhile, the ‘good versus bad Taliban’ strategy has crumbled as the TTA regime in Kabul refuses to stop TTP attacks and has begun cultivating ties with India. According to the Pakistani government and the military establishment, the emergency in KP will sideline the PTI-led provincial administration, paving the way for a decisive military operation against the TTP that will be able to counter proxies backed by the TTA and India more effectively. Emergencies are often viewed as dents in a democratic system. Indeed, but here I would explore it from another angle. There are political scientists, legal scholars and economists who have long observed that structural emergencies frequently act as catalysts for institutional growth. By fracturing rigid bureaucracies, overriding legislative inertia, regulating politicised security institutions and mobilising state capacity, there is a history of emergency conditions that have spurred economic advancement and curbed security threats. In The Political Economy of States of Emergency, legal scholar Balakrishnan Rajagopal demonstrates that economic and national security emergencies historically drive states to centralise financial governance, rationalise labour markets and establish resilient public safety nets. Complementing this, the American sociologist Mancur Olson argued that emergencies dismantle entrenched interest groups. These groups slow down economic growth and facilitate agitation. A clear historical example of this occurred during India’s 21-month emergency (1975–1977), declared by prime minister Indira Gandhi. Prior to the declaration, India was experiencing severe economic stagflation, spiralling inflation driven by global oil shocks, constant industrial strikes and political violence. As documented by the American legal historian Granville Austin, the centralisation of executive power through the emergency enabled the enforcement of a 20-point programme, clamping down on hoarding and strikes, which rapidly reduced inflation, increased industrial production and elevated tax compliance through stringent enforcement. Violence against the state and government too decreased significantly. Illustration by Abro In South Korea, the state of emergency following the Korean War in the 1950s allowed state planners to initiate rapid, export-led industrialisation that transformed a devastated nation into a global economic power. In his book Constitutional Dictatorship, American political scientist Clinton Rossiter argued that temporary emergency powers are necessary mechanisms designed precisely to preserve constitutional order during existential threats. According to Rossiter, far from destroying the legal framework, well-regulated emergency powers allow democracies to deploy decisive force to restore order without permanent constitutional erosion. In Singapore, early post-independence security emergencies led to the establishment of streamlined administrative and judicial frameworks that laid the foundation for one of the world’s most stable, low-crime and commercially reliable legal environments. According to Austin, in India, periods of national emergency eventually led the judiciary to refine constitutional protections, such as establishing the “basic structure doctrine” to balance executive emergency authority with civil liberties. This structural tightening creates a durable framework that lowers everyday crime rates and clarifies rule-of-law standards after the crisis subsides. Emergencies also provide governments with the operational flexibility required to dismantle sophisticated clandestine networks, disrupt their financial channels and re-establish state sovereignty over ungoverned spaces. In Inside Terrorism, American political scientist Bruce Hoffman highlights that anti-terror operations require agility that standard peacetime administrative frameworks rarely afford. Emergencies enable real-time inter-agency intelligence-sharing and rapid response deployments, severely restricting the operational space of militant groups. The contemporary application of this dynamic can be seen in Pakistan’s emergency declaration in KP under Articles 232, 234 and 235. Counter-militancy efforts in KP faced institutional paralysis due to political misalignment between the federal government in Islamabad and PTI’s provincial administration over kinetic military offensives. The Pakistani scholar Hasan Askari Rizvi notes that emergency interventions serve as critical mechanisms for the state to reassert control over volatile territories. By placing executive authority under federal direction, emergency rule allows the federal government to streamline intelligence sharing between military assets and local police, eliminate political opposition to targeted offensives against militant groups and redirect provincial budgetary resources directly into border security and counter-militancy infrastructure. A classic empirical parallel is Peru’s invocation of emergency measures in the early 1990s, which gave law enforcement the extraordinary legal tools necessary to capture the notorious militant leader Abimael Guzmán and effectively neutralise his violent ‘Shining Path’ insurgency. Similarly, France’s 2015 emergency created integrated counter-terrorism intelligence databases and administrative search powers that permanently improved the state’s capacity to disrupt terror plots, while the UK’s security provisions during the conflict between Irish militants and the state in the 1970s and 1980s were eventually codified into permanent frameworks, such as the Terrorism Act 2000. Knee-jerk reactions to emergency/governor rule in KP are expected. New conditions should be tracked and monitored instead of being outrightly rejected through typical social media outrage. For the state and government, it is important to learn from examples in which emergencies not only helped streamline economies and curb violence but also contributed in strengthening democracy in the long run. Published in Dawn, EOS, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Économie russe : les dépenses publiques se rapprochent de la moyenne de l’OCDE
items.description: Selon Alexandre Isakov, directeur du Centre de recherches macroéconomiques de Sber et économiste en chef de la banque publique de développement Vnesheconombank (VEB), les dépenses du budget consolidé de la Russie représenteraient environ 39 % du PIB, soit un niveau proche de la moyenne des pays membres de l’OCDE (42,6 % en 2023) Александр Исаков — РБК : « Экономика России — в стадии принятия новой себя », RBC , 15 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Isakov note que la part du budget dans le PIB de la Russie a considérablement augmenté ces dernières années. En 2018-2019, soit avant le lancement de l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine, les dépenses du budget consolidé représentaient environ un tiers du PIB (32 à 33 % selon Isakov). Cette part aurait ainsi progressé de plus de 6 points entre 2018 et 2025, alors qu’elle n’a gagné qu’environ 2,4 points pour l’OCDE entre 2018 et 2023. L’écart entre la Russie et les pays de l’OCDE se situe aujourd’hui à 3,3 points (sur la base des chiffres de 2023 pour l’OCDE), contre près de 10 points en 2011. La Russie s’approcherait ainsi de la limite supérieure de la taille du secteur public compatible avec des taux de croissance élevés et durables. Selon Isakov, le franchissement du seuil de 40 % pèserait sur les entreprises, l’investissement et sur la capacité du budget à collecter les impôts. Il estime en effet que les entreprises russes reportent déjà leurs investissements en raison de l’incertitude fiscale et du risque macroéconomique, ce qui réduit la demande et la base fiscale potentielle de l’État. Cette incertitude est alimentée par les hausses d’impôts successives destinées à financer l’augmentation des dépenses publiques : l’impôt sur les bénéfices est passé de 20 à 25 % en 2025, la TVA de 20 à 22 % le 1er janvier 2026. La hausse des dépenses de l’État russe est principalement alimentée par le budget de la défense, qui devrait bondir de 32 % en 2027 pour atteindre 17 100 milliards de roubles (environ 182 milliards d’euros). D’ici la fin de l’année, les dépenses militaires russes pourraient ainsi dépasser les 10 % du PIB pour la première fois depuis l’époque soviétique. Le niveau élevé des dépenses publiques dans les pays de l’OCDE, et notamment dans ceux qui sont également membres de l’Union européenne, où la moyenne atteint 49,2 % du PIB (contre 42,6 % en moyenne dans l’OCDE en 2023 et 39 % en Russie en 2025), s’explique principalement par le poids de la protection sociale. La part du PIB consacrée aux dépenses sociales, à la santé et à l’éducation représente en effet environ 27 % dans les pays de l’OCDE (13,4 % pour la protection sociale, 8,4 % pour la santé et 4,9 % pour l’éducation), et 31 % dans ceux de l’Union européenne, contre 19 % en Russie en 2021, selon nos calculs à partir des données du ministère des Finances. L’article Économie russe : les dépenses publiques se rapprochent de la moyenne de l’OCDE est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Ouagadougou / Arrondissement 12 : L’école du mérite célébrée en modèle de citoyenneté
items.description: Les officiels lors de l'exécution de l'hymne national avant le début de la cérémonie relative à la journée de l'excellence scolaire à l'arrondissement 12 C'est une matinée qui aura marqué les esprits dans l'arrondissement 12 de Ouagadougou. Ce 14 octobre 2026, l'arrondissement 12 a vibré au rythme de la cinquième édition de la Journée de l'excellence scolaire, une célébration qui dépasse le simple rituel scolaire pour s'affirmer comme un véritable acte de patriotisme. Placée sous le thème « Célébrer l'excellence scolaire, reconnaître le mérite et promouvoir une culture de la réussite dans l'arrondissement 12 », la cérémonie a voulu rappeler une conviction essentielle : il n'y a pas de nation forte sans école forte, ni de développement durable sans culture du mérite. Les élèves ont répondu présent à la 5e journée de l'excellence scolaire à l'arrondissement 12 Dès les premières heures, le ton a été donné par l'exécution solennelle du Ditanyè, entonné avec ferveur et repris en chœur par des centaines d'élèves en acclamation. Un moment de communion républicaine qui a planté le décor d'une journée dédiée à l'effort et à l'exemplarité. Présidée par Zalissa Salembéré / Paré, présidente de la délégation spéciale de l'arrondissement 12, la cérémonie était placée sous le parrainage de Rasmané Konvolbo, PDG du groupe d'alimentation Bon Samaritain, et le co-parrainage de Souleymane Boly, représentant d'Endeavour Mining. Deux acteurs économiques qui ont fait le choix d'investir dans le capital le plus précieux : le capital humain. La présidente de la délégation spéciale, Zalissa SALEMBERE/ PARE a salué la performance scolaire au sein de son arrondissement et a exhorté les élèves à maintenir le cap Et le message est passé. En distinguant les meilleurs élèves mais aussi les enseignants les plus méritants, l'arrondissement 12 a voulu consacrer le travail bien fait comme valeur cardinale. Vélos pour faciliter la mobilité scolaire, kits complets et tableaux d'honneur ont été remis aux lauréats sous les ovations d'une foule conquise, comme autant d'invitations à persévérer. Au nom des récipiendaires, Mariam Haya a pris la parole avec une maturité qui a forcé l'admiration. Elle a pris l'engagement, au nom de tous les lauréats, de continuer à travailler avec ardeur pour honorer leurs écoles, leurs familles et tout l'arrondissement. Parrain de l'événement, Rasmané Konvolbo a salué une initiative qui fonde l'avenir sur le mérite, la responsabilité et le travail. Pour le PDG de Bon Samaritain, célébrer l'excellence, c'est préparer une société plus juste et plus forte. Il a félicité l'arrondissement 12 pour sa constance et réaffirmé sa disponibilité à accompagner durablement toute initiative qui place l'éducation au cœur du progrès collectif. Plusieurs lots dont des vélos ont été remis aux élèves méritants La présidente de la délégation spéciale n'a pas caché, elle non plus, sa fierté. Zalissa Salembéré / Paré a tenu à ancrer cette journée comme un levier de développement et non comme une simple fête. Chiffres à l'appui, elle a démontré la dynamique ascendante de la circonscription : sur 1 420 candidats présentés dont 720 filles, 1 095 admis au Certificat d'études primaires, soit un taux de succès de 98,24% contre 95,28% en 2025. Mieux, 31 écoles ont réalisé un sans-faute avec 100% de réussite. Une performance qui hisse l'arrondissement 12 au rang de deuxième meilleure performance scolaire de la commune de Ouagadougou. En s'adressant aux lauréats, elle les a invités à l'humilité et à la constance dans l'apprentissage, tout en ayant un mot d'encouragement pour ceux qui n'ont pas été distingués cette année : l'excellence est un chemin, pas une ligne d'arrivée. Elle a salué le rôle irremplaçable des enseignants et des parents d'élèves, véritables artisans de cette réussite, et témoigné sa gratitude au patron de la cérémonie, le président de la délégation spéciale de la commune, aux parrains, au comité d'organisation et à tous les acteurs mobilisés. La fête s'est achevée en beauté, entre animations culturelles et remise solennelle des prix, sous les applaudissements nourris du public. Plus qu'une cérémonie de récompense, l'arrondissement 12 vient de donner une leçon : quand l'école célèbre le mérite, c'est toute la nation qui se met debout. L’article Ouagadougou / Arrondissement 12 : L'école du mérite célébrée en modèle de citoyenneté est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Arguments sought on defamation suit against PTI founder
items.description: LAHORE: A sessions court on Saturday sought arguments from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s counsel on a miscellaneous application by a lawyer for PTI founding chairman Imran Khan seeking permission to meet his client in jail regarding a Rs10 billion defamation suit filed by the former against the latter. Earlier, Khan’s counsel, Muhammad Hussain Chotia, argued for permission to meet his client at Adiala Jail, Rawalpindi, saying he needed instructions from him regarding the case and his signatures on documents. He told the court that the jail authorities were not allowing the meeting. He asked the court to direct the jail superintendent to permit him to meet Khan. Additional District & Sessions Judge Yalmaz Ghani adjourned the hearing till Oct 31 and sought arguments from the prime minister’s lawyer. In his suit filed in 2017, Prime Minister Shehbaz said Imran Khan levelled baseless allegations against him in connection with the Panama Papers controversy. He sought a decree for recovery of Rs10bn as compensation from the defendant for publication of defamatory content. Several key government figures, including Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Ahmad Khan have already recorded their statements in support of the plaintiff, the prime minister. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

Son los términos que han utilizado algunos de los involucrados en las negociaciones para la unión de la izquierda a la izquierda del PSOE al describir el proceso. Los múltiples llamamientos en medios de comunicación y redes sociales para “estar a la altura de la responsabilidad histórica” y responder a “lo que pide la gente” derivaron en reproches mutuos y han concluido en una foto engañosa que tiene más que ver con las expectativas generadas que con las posibilidades reales. En último término, como resume el politólogo Pablo Simón, “se trataba de un juego de incentivos en el que cada formación debía decidir qué quería: maximizar la representación, es decir, que hubiese más tarta para repartir entre todos, o proteger o reflotar la propia marca”. La respuesta a esa pregunta explica, en gran parte, el desenlace de esas conversaciones. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Rufián, el gran prestidigitador
items.description: La ilusión se encendió en la sala Galileo Galilei, en Madrid, el pasado 18 de febrero. El portavoz de Esquerra Republicana en el Congreso, Gabriel Rufián (Santa Coloma de Gramenet, 44 años), tras siete meses de declaraciones en defensa de una suma de la izquierda alternativa para confrontar a las derechas, parecía dar un paso más allá. Su sintonía con Podemos, especialmente con Irene Montero, era conocida. Pero que la puesta de largo de su propuesta fuera justamente el diputado autonómico por Más Madrid Emilio Delgado hizo pensar a muchos que algo diferente estaba en gestación. ¿Podría la magia de Rufián unir lo roto en 2019, con el cisma entre Pablo Iglesias e Íñigo Errejón? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un frente de izquierdas y otro de derechas se disputarán a cara de perro el control del Senado
items.description: El Senado no será un campo de batalla secundario sino central en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. Mientras en el Congreso, las distintas opciones políticas concurrirán por separado —muchas fuerzas a la izquierda del PSOE se han agrupado en el llamado Frente Amplio, del que se han excluido Podemos y los nacionalistas catalanes, vascos o gallegos—, en el Senado se están configurando dos bloques mayoritarios, una de derechas y otro de izquierdas, enfrentados a cara de perro. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Aitor Esteban: “Nadie ha demostrado más con hechos que no queremos a Vox”
items.description: Desde hace meses, Aitor Esteban (Bilbao, 64 años) venía advirtiendo de que al Gobierno de coalición se le acababa el combustible. Hace dos semanas, 48 horas antes de que el Congreso tumbase los decretos de vivienda , el presidente del PNV viajó a Madrid y ya barruntaba en privado que Pedro Sánchez podría estar sopesando la convocatoria electoral , aun en el caso de que ganase las votaciones. “Para él era como cambiar de ventana después de que todo estuviese centrado en Ceuta”, comentaba Esteban el pasado viernes en Sabin Etxea, la sede central del PNV en Bilbao. “La legislatura tenía que tener un propósito, no gobernar por gobernar, solo resistir. Ya no tenía sentido”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los dos grandes creen que la campaña se va colocando donde querían
items.description: Al ver las imágenes de Pedro Sánchez bailando eufórico al final del gran mitin de consagración de su candidatura en Fuenlabrada, la pregunta surge natural: ¿tan convencido está el líder del PSOE de que puede repetir el milagro de 2023 y seguir en La Moncloa? Según distintas personas de su entorno consultadas, no se trata de una pose, aunque todo candidato está obligado a trasladar entusiasmo si quiere que le voten. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El colosal reto de evaluar a los universitarios en la era de la IA: ¿prohibirla o usarla como aliada?
items.description: Mucho ha llovido en la prestigiosa Universidad de Brown (Estados Unidos) desde que su catedrático Roberto Serrano denunciase en este diario en junio un fraude masivo con inteligencia artificial (IA) en uno de sus exámenes, sin que el decanato reaccionase. La noticia fue replicada por los principales medios ―hasta la revista Nature le pidió un artículo―, Serrano ha recibido “cientos” de cartas de apoyo y la persona que estaba al frente del Comité del Código Académico ha sido cesada. Pero lo que más conmueve al eminente economista español es que cree que sus alumnos han aprendido la lección. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Gabriel Rufián es un genio
items.description: Lo mínimo que puede decirse de Gabriel Rufián es que es un genio. Desde hace meses, según los estudios de opinión, el portavoz de Esquerra Republicana aparece como el político más valorado y al que se deseaba como aglutinador del frente de guerra de guerrillas que ha demostrado ser la infantil izquierda a la izquierda. Lo ha conseguido a pesar de una doble paradoja. La primera tiene que ver con su vinculación al proyecto que lo creó y catapultó: no es fácil descifrar cómo un independentista ha engatusado a un votante concienciado de Malasaña, haciéndole olvidar que su principal objetivo, en teoría, era conseguir la secesión de una de las regiones más ricas de España, con lo que quebraría la solidaridad interterritorial. A la vez, segunda paradoja, su dominio de las redes sociales de segunda generación ha actuado como un somnífero viral que ha logrado borrar de la memoria un episodio clave de su actividad parlamentaria. Él ―ese hombre de la calle que se atreve a decir las verdades en comisiones de investigación y la tribuna del Congreso― fue el dirigente que más seriamente puso en riesgo la iniciativa social más determinante de los gobiernos de Pedro Sánchez: la reforma laboral. En aquella ocasión su ángel de la guarda fue un diputado popular que se confundió al votar. Pero si el no defendido entonces por Rufián hubiese tumbado aquella reforma consensuada por el Ministerio de Trabajo con los agentes sociales, ¿habría logrado culminar la exitosa transformación de su personaje? Lo dudo. Pero sería un error infravalorarlo. Hace cuatro días ha conseguido llegar a un pacto con Podemos, a pesar de que el partido de Pablo Iglesias fue claro al valorar el principal proyecto de Esquerra Republicana de esta legislatura en Cataluña. “Nace muerta”, sentenció Ione Belarra, sobre la reforma del modelo de financiación. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Hermana, no es la ideología
items.description: Hace un tiempo, el psiquiatra mallorquín Miquel Roca y yo anduvimos fantaseando con hacer retratos de orden psicológico a figuras políticas. Todo fluía, con humor incluso, con personajes del pasado, pero llegábamos al presente y, ay, se corría el peligro de patologizar cualquier comportamiento. Escudriñar la mente, el corazón o el intestino (allá donde quiera que se refugie la ética) puede llevarte de la comprensión al perdón, o de la admiración al desprecio. En el crudo ambiente político que vivimos, los hay que hacen pinitos psicologistas con brocha gorda: abundan, por ejemplo, aquellos que acusan al presidente Sánchez de defender los principios de igualdad y fraternidad sobre los que se construyó la Europa nacida de la Segunda Guerra Mundial movido únicamente por la espuria intención de revitalizar su imagen ante la izquierda desmovilizada. Es decir, que más que luchar por el bien común, el ladino presidente estaría batallando por seguir gozando del célebre Falcon. Si así fuera, si aceptamos que Sánchez defiende lo que es justo movido por una ambición desmedida, no me encuentro en condiciones de juzgarlo, porque, hoy, es más urgente la misión política que la sinceridad del jugador. ¿Cómo llegamos a su mente, corazón o intestino? ¿con el célebre polígrafo? Además ¿de qué serviría? Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Gran Reemplazo europeo
items.description: ¿Recuerdan cuando la UE reconvenía a estados como Hungría o Polonia cuando sus gobiernos recortaban derechos, cuando debatíamos cómo controlar sus desmanes iliberales? Esta semana, en el Consejo Europeo celebrado en Bruselas, la primera ministra danesa, la socialdemócrata Mette Frederiksen, con el respaldo entusiasta de la posfascista Giorgia Meloni, invirtió de forma oficial esa lógica al pedir que se examinara a España no por recortar derechos, sino por reconocérselos a medio millón de personas mediante un proceso de regularización. Esa inversión dice mucho sobre el estado de la Unión, pues Europa servía precisamente para proteger los derechos individuales frente a las mayorías y acervos nacionales, mientras hoy, de forma falaz, cuando nadie puede afirmar que la regularización viole norma alguna, se apuesta abiertamente por una política migratoria , mayoritaria en Europa, donde los derechos, pensados para no someterse a votación, pueden revisarse y cercenarse cuando así lo quieren nuestros gobiernos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El debate de las pensiones entra en terreno pantanoso: ¿hay que reformar el modelo o cambiarlo por otro?
items.description: Desde el adelanto electoral al 29 de noviembre, el debate sobre las pensiones ha irrumpido con fuerza en la precampaña. El diputado de Vox, José María Figaredo, ha llegado a afirmar que “ el sistema de pensiones es un zombi . Lo han quebrado” y que “en casi 30 años no se ha aplicado ninguna medida correctora”, pese a las sucesivas reformas aprobadas desde 1996, entre ellas el retraso de la edad de jubilación a los 67 años, los cambios en el cálculo de la pensión o los mecanismos introducidos para contener el gasto y elevar los ingresos del sistema. Figaredo también defendió “ una reforma estructural hacia un modelo mixto que combine el reparto con la capitalización individual, como han hecho con éxito otros países europeos”, si bien los países con mayor peso de la capitalización mantienen sistemas públicos de pensiones y no los han privatizado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La solución a la crisis de vivienda no es (solo) construir más
items.description: Hay una generación de jóvenes, nacida alrededor del cambio de siglo, que prácticamente solo ha vivido de crisis en crisis, lanzada por el destino a una sacudida tan violenta como una catarata. Esa generación empieza a levantar la voz. El canario en la mina fueron l os abucheos de los universitarios estadounidenses a los discursos triunfalistas sobre la IA. La rabia de los estudiantes franceses ha puesto el país patas arriba; en Italia hay miles de jóvenes movilizados; Bélgica prepara una huelga por los recortes en sanidad y educación. La ola de contestación juvenil golpea por las más diversas causas: al Sur de los Pirineos la razón es lo que el escritor Manuel Rivas ha bautizado como “violencia catastral”. Una profunda crisis inmobiliaria espoleada por el desahucio de una octogenaria, el caso Maricarmen , ha acabado provocando una convocatoria de huelga general y un adelanto electoral. La solución va para largo, pero las recetas se han colado en campaña y son fáciles de resumir. Las izquierdas proponen regular ante un fallo de mercado clamoroso, y ocho de cada 10 españoles quieren que el Estado intervenga. Las derechas plantean construir más: laissez faire . Regular no va a arreglarlo todo de un día para otro, pero construir lo suficiente para desatascar el problema es, simple y llanamente, imposible a corto plazo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El todopoderoso alcalde que llevó al PP a una crisis anunciada en Algeciras
items.description: Una señora mayor con el brazo escayolado reconoce al todavía alcalde de Algeciras (Cádiz) y exsenador del PP, José Ignacio Landaluce, en una plaza del centro de la ciudad gaditana este viernes. Se acerca a él con pasitos cortos: “He visto todo lo que está saliendo en la tele y quiero que sepas que no me creo nada”, le dice con una sonrisa. Landaluce le devuelve el gesto, le da las gracias y le lanza un beso. La mujer alude a las denuncias presentadas por dos afiliadas del PP por presuntas agresiones sexuales contra el dirigente. Unas horas después de ese encuentro, el Juzgado de Violencia sobre la Mujer de Algeciras cita a Landaluce para declarar como imputado el próximo 23 de octubre por una de ellas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El despido de la portavoz de Trump desliza a la Casa Blanca hacia el caos a dos semanas de las ‘midterms’
items.description: La segunda presidencia de Donald Trump, se dijo, no iba a ser como la primera. Él llegaba tras una travesía en el desierto, pero con las lecciones aprendidas; rodeado de un ejército de fieles, y no, como en 2017, de un equipo de colaboradores dispuestos a llevarle la contraria de vez en cuando. Tampoco sería, como sí fue aquella, un incesante espectáculo de filtraciones, puñaladas entre bambalinas y despidos impulsivos a golpe de tuit. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Álex Corretja: “Una de las cosas más importantes del tenis y de la vida es saber borrar lo que acaba de suceder”
items.description: París, 10 de junio de 2001. Un tenista entra furioso en el vestuario en mitad de la final que está jugando en Roland Garros . Ha enviado un revés ganador fuera por un “puto centímetro” que hubiera roto el servicio de su rival y, de ganar su saque, ponerse dos sets arriba en el partido. Pero el set ha volado y ahora la final está en lo mejor: uno a uno. El tenista es Álex Corretja , que perdió la final del año anterior ante Carlos Moyá . Ha llegado de nuevo, esta vez contra el brasileño Guga Kuerten. La preparación ha sido absoluta. En lugar de hacer la pretemporada en diciembre, la hizo en enero. Se fue a Sierra Nevada para correr en altura y aumentar glóbulos rojos; se llevó un sparring, un colega para correr con él de liebre, preparador físico, entrenador, médicos, nutricionista. Todo enfocado a Roland Garros. Y ahora, con empate en el marcador, se mira al espejo y dice: “No vas a conseguir ganar nunca este puto torneo”. Sale a la pista y Kuerten le mete 6-2 / 6-0 en los dos siguientes sets. Seguir leyendo Estilismo: Ángela Esteban-Librero Maquillaje: David López (Another Artists Agency) Producción: Cristina Serrano Asistente de fotografía: Miguel Sancho Asistente de estilismo: Lidia Lara Asistente de producción: Marina Marco

items.title: Peter Thiel, el tecnoligarca que cree en el anticristo
items.description: Cuando Hulk Hogan demandó al medio sensacionalista Gawker en 2016 por la publicación sin su consentimiento de un vídeo de contenido sexual, nadie daba un duro por él. Pero Hogan ganó el juicio y consiguió una indemnización de 140 millones de dólares que acabó con la publicación online . Peter Thiel , uno de los personajes más siniestros de Silicon Valley, decantó la batalla judicial: financió en secreto a los abogados de Hogan. Quería vengarse de Gawker porque lo había ridiculizado durante años y desvelado su homosexualidad. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bastaría con querer hacerlo
items.description: Desde luego no ha sido la primera vez que sucede algo así, ni, por desgracia, era inesperado, pero el rechazo de los decretos de vivienda ha vuelto a dejarme anonadada. Se ve que las fuerzas políticas de nuestro país son incapaces de colaborar en causas esenciales, tan esenciales, en fin, que van mucho más allá de los valores partidistas y son transversales, afectando a toda la sociedad, sea cual sea su ideología. No digo que los decretos fueran perfectos ni suficientes. Todo es susceptible de mejora. Pero usar la catástrofe habitacional para arreciar en el pimpampum electoralista y politiquero me parece deprimente (además de que deben de estar sordos y miopes, dada la indignación que arde en las calles). Seguir leyendo

items.title: Medio centenar de fortificaciones en Gaza: así toma Israel el control de la Franja
items.description: Alrededor de las enormes fortificaciones que Israel ha levantado en Gaza no queda nada. Algunas de ellas se remontan a 2023, tras los atentados de Hamás aquel 7 de octubre y la posterior invasión de la Franja por parte de Israel. Pero la construcción de nuevos puestos se ha acelerado a partir del alto el fuego del 10 de octubre de 2025: al menos 15 de ellos aparecen por primera vez en imágenes de satélite en diciembre del año pasado. “Estos puestos sirven como bases a través de las cuales Israel mantiene y ejerce control territorial sobre Gaza”, asegura Sarah Sanbar , investigadora de la ONG Human Rights Watch (HRW). Seguir leyendo Metodología Para localizar las fortificaciones militares israelíes en Gaza, hemos desarrollado un sistema de búsqueda visual basado en inteligencia artificial que nos ha permitido identificar estructuras similares entre cientos de imágenes de satélite. Después, hemos revisado y contrastado los resultados para distinguir las posiciones fortificadas de otras construcciones o movimientos de tierra. En total, hemos analizado más de 600 imágenes de la Franja de Gaza, tomadas entre enero de 2023 y octubre de 2026, que suman más de 400 GB de información. La mayoría proceden de Planet Labs y tienen una resolución aproximada de medio metro por píxel. También hemos utilizado una imagen aérea del norte de Gaza, publicada en la plataforma GovMap del Gobierno de Israel, con una resolución aproximada de 15 centímetros por píxel. La investigación se ha desarrollado en cinco fases, con sucesivas rondas de búsqueda y revisión: 1. Selección de ejemplos . Escogimos 15 imágenes de fortificaciones con características reconocibles: grandes muros de tierra, accesos protegidos, zanjas y estructuras interiores como barracones, vehículos o antenas. Añadimos otros 15 ejemplos de caminos, excavaciones y terrenos arrasados que podían confundirse con ellas. 2. Búsqueda mediante inteligencia artificial . Dividimos las imágenes en 1.550.108 fragmentos, procedentes de 602 escenas de Planet Labs y de la imagen aérea de GovMap. Desarrollamos una herramienta que comparó estos fragmentos con los ejemplos seleccionados y los ordenó según su similitud. Repetimos las búsquedas incorporando los resultados ya revisados para identificar nuevos candidatos. La inteligencia artificial nos ayudó a localizar posibles fortificaciones, pero no decidió cuáles lo eran. 3. Revisión y evolución temporal . Examinamos las propuestas, descartamos las coincidencias incorrectas y reunimos imágenes de distintas fechas para cada ubicación. Así pudimos reconstruir los cambios visibles en el terreno y observar cuándo aparecían las primeras modificaciones. 4. Comprobación de uso militar. Para distinguir las fortificaciones de otros recintos, buscamos indicios adicionales, especialmente estructuras compatibles con barracones o módulos prefabricados. Revisamos distintas fechas para comprobar si estas instalaciones habían estado presentes, incluso cuando el recinto aparecía posteriormente vacío. Estos elementos, junto con la configuración del terreno, reforzaron la identificación de las posiciones militares. 5. Recuento final . Tras descartar falsos positivos y agrupar las imágenes correspondientes a una misma ubicación, identificamos 50 posiciones fortificadas. Para documentar su evolución, elaboramos 50 series temporales con 4.382 imágenes, accesibles para los lectores de EL PAÍS, después de excluir los recortes sin cobertura suficiente. Limitaciones de la investigación . La cobertura de las imágenes no es uniforme: no disponemos de todos los lugares en todas las fechas. Por eso, la primera imagen en la que aparece una construcción no indica necesariamente cuándo fue levantada. Las 50 posiciones identificadas representan las fortificaciones que hemos podido verificar en el material disponible, no un censo exhaustivo de todas las existentes en Gaza. Aunque hemos revisado miles de candidatos, no podemos descartar que haya otras posiciones que nuestra herramienta no haya detectado. Las imágenes nos permiten documentar las estructuras y su evolución, pero no determinar por sí solas la función exacta de cada instalación ni si estuvo ocupada de manera continua. Para ello necesitamos contrastar nuestras observaciones con otras fuentes.

items.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats, beat up French mayor
items.description: JERUSALEM: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy of European diplomats and beat up a visiting French mayor, in a new escalation of violence during the Palestinian olive harvest, witnesses and diplomats said. The 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France, kicked him and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the occupied West Bank alongside the top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats. “I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, said after he was attacked. “The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said. “For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.” Baudoux, who was wearing a sash with the French tricolour, was seen collapsed on the side of the car after the attack but he did not need hospital care. The mayor, wearing a blue, white and red sash, leans against a vehicle as masked men intercept and surround a car at a village in the occupied West Bank. —AFP The attack came just one day after settlers beat an American photographer for The Washington Post, who was in moderate condition with broken vertebrae on Saturday. Israel’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation. But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, days away from an election in which he is seeking to shore up support from the far-right, instead alleged a “smear” campaign against settlers. Netanyahu said the diplomats should have coordinated their movements with the Israeli military and pointed out that Baudoux is a communist known for supporting the Palestinian cause. “We urge caution before drawing conclusions” about the attacks, Netanyahu’s office said in a statement. His main rival in the Oct 27 elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, strongly criticised Netanyahu over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the State of Israel still possesses”. The attacks are “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”, Eisenkot said. Belgium called for an end to “impunity for violent settlers” after the latest attack. Attacks on cultural symbol Baudoux, the mayor, said he had come to the town of Taybeh, a Christian stronghold, along with his local pastor from France to sign a goodwill agreement. He was attacked just as he joined the harvest as a symbolic gesture with the Palestinians, for whom olives are an important cultural symbol. Extremist Israelis have issued calls to stop the Palestinians’ harvest after months of growing attacks in which settlers have stolen land and property. There has also been violence against Israelis, with a Palestinian shooting dead a settler last month. Bashar Fawadleh, a priest in Taybeh, said settlers had already attacked the harvest and snatched olives before beating the mayor. “One person was hit in the head and needed stitches. They also beat up an older lady in her 70s after insulting her with very bad words,” the pastor said. The West Bank violence has shocked much of the world, with Britain leading economic sanctions that in turn caused Netanyahu to voice outrage. Netanyahu had also sought to throw doubt on the circumstances behind the beating of the photographer, Heidi Levine, alleging that Palestinians and “far-left” activists caused trouble. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Tanger : le FITUT revient pour sa 19è édition
items.description: La 19e édition du Festival international du théâtre universitaire de Tanger (FITUT) se tiendra du 26 au 30 octobre. Ce rendez-vous culturel et artistique vise à promouvoir la création théâtrale universitaire, à favoriser les échanges artistiques et culturels entre étudiants et professionnels et à valoriser le théâtre en tant qu’espace d’expression, de créativité et de dialogue entre les cultures, indique un communiqué des organisateurs. Cette manifestation ambitionne également de contribuer au rayonnement culturel et artistique de la ville de Tanger, en mettant en valeur les initiatives théâtrales universitaires et en favorisant l’ouverture sur différentes expériences artistiques et culturelles. Le jury de cette édition est composé de figures du théâtre et du paysage artistique marocain, notamment l’écrivain et metteur en scène El Meskini Sghir, les actrices Naïma Elias et Hajar Alsharki, ainsi que l’acteur Abderrahim El Meniari. Le programme prévoit une série de représentations au Palais des Arts et de la Culture et dans d’autres espaces de la ville, avec la participation d’établissements et d’institutions artistiques du Maroc, d’Espagne, de Pologne, d’Oman, des Pays-Bas, d’Arabie saoudite, du Portugal, d’Arménie et d’Italie. En parallèle des spectacles, des ateliers théâtraux et des séances d’échange et de débat à l’issue des représentations sont prévus, afin de favoriser les interactions entre les équipes artistiques et le public. À travers cette programmation, le FITUT entend consolider la place du théâtre universitaire comme espace de rencontre, de création et de dialogue interculturel, tout en contribuant au rayonnement culturel et artistique de Tanger. The post Tanger : le FITUT revient pour sa 19è édition appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Balochistan CM Bugti urges Fazl to keep national security above politics
items.description: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti has said that law and order and national security in Balochistan should be treated as issues beyond political differences. He stressed that comparisons between the governments of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, particularly regarding terrorism and national security, must be based on ground realities and practical measures. The chief minister said he holds JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in high regard and that their personal relationship is based on mutual respect. In a statement posted on social media platform X, CM Bugti said the Maulana and his party had also been targeted in terrorist attacks. He expressed the hope that the JUI-F chief would take into account the state’s efforts to combat terrorism and the sacrifices made by security forces when commenting on this sensitive national issue. CM Bugti said the performance of the two provincial governments should be assessed on the basis of their counterterrorism measures, the conduct of their political leadership, and their commitment to eliminating terrorism. He said that despite political differences between the government and opposition in Balochistan, both sides had maintained a common position against terrorism, demonstrating a commitment to placing national interests above partisan considerations. The chief minister said his government regularly took the opposition into confidence on counterterrorism strategies, key decisions, and related matters in the Balochistan Assembly. He added that the provincial government was committed to taking all parliamentary parties along. He cited acknowledgements by Opposition Leader Mir Younis Aziz Zehri and a recent speech by Balochistan National Party (Mengal) parliamentary leader Mir Jahanzeb Mengal as evidence of the province’s political leadership recognising its responsibility in the fight against terrorism. CM Bugti said the JUI-F, the National Party, the BNP-Mengal, and other parliamentary parties shared a common stance against terrorism. He stressed that the fight against terrorism was not merely a matter of political statements or claims but a shared res­p­­o­­nsibility of the state and the entire nation. Pakistan, he said, was continuing its eff­­­orts to eliminate terrorism, while off­i­cers and personnel of the Pakistan Ar­­­­my and other security institutions were making extraordinary sacrifices in the struggle. Describing Maulana Fazlur Rehman as a senior politician whose party had also suffered human and political losses due to terrorism, CM Bugti said comparisons between the governments of KP and Balochistan must consider their practical counterterrorism measures, coordination among political leaders, and cooperation with state institutions. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Egypt ‘ready to defend’ Saudi Arabia against Houthis
items.description: • President Sisi says Cairo will take ‘any measure’ to protect kingdom if asked • Iran backs ‘political process’, offers to mediate • Saudi, Houthi forces trade fire CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi pledged on Saturday that Egypt was ready to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi forces if requested, as fighting intensified across the region and Cairo moved towards possible parliamentary authorisation for support. Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy, Sisi said Egypt was “not looking for a role to play” in regional conflicts but that it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was “harmed or its security and stability threatened”. “Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you,” Sisi said. He said any deployment would require parliamentary approval and expressed hope lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to authorise support “if it is requested of us”. “I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone,” Sisi said. “We are speaking only about defence.” Egyptian state media later reported that parliament would hold an emergency session on Sunday at Sisi’s request to consider possible support for Saudi defences. Egypt joined the Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen in 2015, though its role has largely focused on securing Red Sea shipping routes rather than frontline combat. The renewed conflict also threatens Egypt’s economic interests, particularly Suez Canal revenues. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last month that the Suez Canal had lost about $11 billion in revenue since the Houthis began attacking commercial vessels in 2023. During a visit to Egypt last month, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea. Egypt has not joined the Makkah agreement, a mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan in August, and has said it is studying the agreement. Sisi also said on Saturday that his presidential term would end in 2030 and proposed a 30-month training programme at the Egyptian Military Academy to prepare potential future leaders. He said a committee would develop selection criteria and legislation for the programme, which would target PhD holders from reputable Egyptian and foreign universities. Iran, meanwhile, backed a political solution to the Saudi-Houthi conflict and renewed its offer to mediate. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi repeated Iran’s offer to mediate between the two sides. Araghchi said on Saturday at the Organ­isation of Islamic Coope­ration in Baghdad that Tehran supported an “incl­usive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue”. Araghchi also said, “Either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together,” adding that Iran was willing to cooperate with its neighbours. Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis’ recent escalation, a charge Tehran denies. The fighting continued on Saturday, with Saudi Arabia saying it intercepted four drones over Riyadh, the Eastern Province and the south. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said the drones were “intercepted and destroyed” as the kingdom faced repeated Houthi missile and drone attacks on oil installations, tankers and airports. Houthi-affiliated med­ia, meanwhile, said Saudi air strikes beginning overnight killed at least 12 people in Yemen, including three children. It said strikes on “civilian homes” in Taiz killed nine people and wounded 16, while attacks in Dhamar killed three children and wounded 17. The Houthi news agency also alleged that Saudi forces used cluster bombs. The Saudi-led coalition did not immediately comment on that claim. The renewed war in Yemen has intensified since July. The Houthis have attacked Saudi energy facilities, vessels and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed last week. The Houthis have also seized territory around the Bab al-Mandab Strait, increasing pressure on Red Sea shipping and energy exports. Separately, the Houthis announced the release of 159 pro-government fighters under an amnesty after their recent territorial gains. The International Committee of the Red Cross confirmed the release and said it helped with interviews, health checks, family contacts and transportation. Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026

items.title: Sharifs invoke security fears to defend KP move
items.description: • PM Shehbaz insists govt was ‘compelled’ to impose emergency and governor’s rule • Says Centre exhausted dialogue before taking measures • Nawaz Sharif stresses decision should have been taken earlier • Accuses PTI of using provincial resources for confrontation LAHORE: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sha­rif and PML-N President Nawaz Sharif on Saturday defended the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with the premier saying the federal government had been “compel­led” to take the step over security conce­rns and the elder Sharif arguing that the intervention should have come much earlier. The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The measures were endorsed by parliament this week amid opposition protests. On Saturday, Shehbaz Sharif visited the residence of Rashid Bashir Virk in Gujranwala to offer condolences over the death of his father, former MNA Mahmood Bashir Virk. After recalling the late PML-N lawmaker’s services, the prime minister said the Centre had made a “last attempt” to avoid imposing emergency, referring to rounds of talks held by a joint government-PPP delegation with the opposition. The second round of talks, held on Oct 3 , lasted several hours but ended without a breakthrough. “They had talks with them (PTI) day and night, for 48 hours, and sat with the intention to settle matters from every aspect,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that a draft agreement had been prepared under which the PTI was to call off its protest march. The prime minister said he had held multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional, as well as with his predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur. “In every meeting, I tried my best to convey to him from the depths of my heart and with seriousness that KP is an extremely beautiful province and has very brave and honourable people, […] and I am always present in every way for their development and prosperity,” the premier said. PM Shehbaz said he had assured the KP government of the Centre’s support in jointly fighting terrorism and addressing security challenges in the province. He added that he had assured the chief minister that decisions regarding administration, resources and requirements would be made in consultation with the provincial government. “But, unfortunately, despite all these efforts, thousands of our law enforcement personnel, soldiers and officers of the armed forces were sacrificing their lives to defend the homeland,” he said. The prime minister said the federal government had made repeated efforts to address the situation but had instead faced “threats and long marches every other day”. The Oct 11 measures followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and PTI, as well as negotiations aimed at bridging differences after the party announced a long march towards Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Nawaz backs governor’s rule Meanwhile, PML-N President Nawaz Sharif on Saturday fully backed the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, saying the measures should have been taken much earlier as the law and order situation deteriorated. Speaking to journalists at his residence in London, Mr Sharif said the situation in KP had become increasingly alarming under the PTI government and that the federal authorities should have intervened before matters worsened further. “This intervention was necessary to restore peace, improve governance and protect the interests of the people,” the former prime minister was quoted as saying by journalist Azhar Javed, who was present in the media talk. Mr Sharif also accused the PTI of using provincial government resources for political confrontation with the federation. “Which country allows a chief minister to use official resources to attack the federal capital?” he asked, questioning the use of provincial resources for political purposes. He accused PTI of damaging the province during its 13 years in power, alleging that successive PTI governments had failed to provide effective governance and neglected the interests of ordinary citizens. Mr Sharif said the people of KP were patriotic Pakistanis who deserved better governance and leadership. Zulqernain Tahir also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, October 18th, 2026
